B05C001.summary: The allied kings gather in Virata's court the morning after Abhimanyu's wedding. Krishna reviews how the Pandavas were cheated at dice, served their exile, and endured the hidden thirteenth year, then argues they ask only for their rightful share. He proposes that a fair envoy be sent to Duryodhana before any war is considered. The chapter sets up the peace effort that drives the rest of the Udyoga Parva.

scenes.B05C001S01: The kings assemble in Virata's court and Krishna lays out the Pandavas' case and proposes sending an envoy to the Kauravas.

shots.B05C001S01H01: Opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Saraswati, before the story begins.
shots.B05C001S01H02: Vaisampayana describes the assembled kings in Virata's court, then Krishna's speech on the Pandavas' treatment and his call for an envoy to seek a peaceful settlement; the paragraph ends with Balarama praising Krishna's words.

B05C002.summary: Balarama answers Krishna by urging peace: the Pandavas will give up half the kingdom, and an envoy should go to Duryodhana and to the elders with humble words. He recalls that Yudhishthira lost at dice through his own unskilled play and that Shakuni was not to blame. Satyaki then rises in anger to attack Balarama's position. The split between the peace party and the war party begins here.

scenes.B05C002S01: Balarama proposes a conciliatory envoy to the Kauravas, and Satyaki rises up in anger to answer him.

shots.B05C002S01H01: Balarama's speech: he backs a peaceful settlement, names the elders and princes the envoy should greet, and recalls the dice game as a reason for humility rather than war.
shots.B05C002S01H02: Vaisampayana notes that Satyaki stands up in indignation while Balarama is still speaking.

B05C003.summary: Satyaki scolds Balarama for speaking softly and says the dice match was a trick, so Yudhishthira has no reason to beg. He vows to force Duryodhana to bow down through battle and lists the Pandava warriors and allies who would fight. He insists that Yudhishthira must get his kingdom back, or the enemy will fall in war. The chapter sharpens the case for war.

scenes.B05C003S01: Satyaki attacks Balarama's plea for peace and declares that the Pandavas must regain their kingdom by force.

shots.B05C003S01H01: Satyaki's speech: he calls Balarama's counsel a reflection of his nature, condemns the dice game as an unfair win, and promises to force the Kauravas to yield through war.

B05C004.summary: Drupada agrees with Satyaki that Duryodhana will not give up the kingdom peacefully. He still thinks the Pandavas should first send a message, but he advises against a mild approach and wants them to gather allies at once. He lists many kings to be called and names a priest to be sent to Dhritarashtra. The chapter shows the war camp beginning to prepare.

scenes.B05C004S01: Drupada rejects a gentle approach to Duryodhana and calls for allies to be summoned while a priest is sent to Dhritarashtra.

shots.B05C004S01H01: Drupada's speech: he doubts Duryodhana will yield, sees a gentle approach as weakness, and lists the kings, by name, whom messengers should summon, along with a priest to carry the message to Dhritarashtra.

B05C005.summary: Krishna responds that the Pandavas' cause is just, but he asks Virata to send a message to the Kauravas before any fighting begins. He says that if the Kuru side refuses peace, the Pandavas will be called and Arjuna will act. Virata honors Krishna and sends him back to Dwaraka. The two camps then gather armies, and the chapter shows the war effort growing.

scenes.B05C005S01: Krishna asks that a peace message be sent to the Kauravas, and Virata sends him home as both camps begin to gather forces.

shots.B05C005S01H01: Krishna's speech: he sees the Pandavas' cause as just, asks that a peaceful message be sent to the Kauravas first, and warns that Arjuna will act if Duryodhana refuses.
shots.B05C005S01H02: Vaisampayana reports that Virata sends Krishna away with honor, that both sides gather forces across the land, and that Drupada sends his priest to the Kauravas.

B05C006.summary: Drupada gives the priest detailed advice on how to approach Dhritarashtra. He says that the old king has knowingly followed his son, and that the envoy should stir up the elders and the soldiers so that the Kauravas lose heart. He tells the priest to leave at an auspicious time, while the Pandavas quietly prepare. The chapter ends with the priest setting out for Hastinapura with his followers.

scenes.B05C006S01: Drupada gives the priest his instructions, and the priest sets out for Hastinapura with his disciples.

shots.B05C006S01H01: Drupada's speech: he ranks living beings, names the priest among the wisest, explains how Dhritarashtra was complicit in the dice cheating, and tells the envoy how to win over the elders and the army before setting out at a lucky hour.
shots.B05C006S01H02: Vaisampayana says that the priest, following Drupada's instructions, sets out for Hastinapura with his disciples to serve the Pandavas.

B05C007.summary: Both Duryodhana and Arjuna travel to Dwaraka to ask Krishna for help in the coming war. Krishna is asleep when they arrive, and Arjuna is the first he sees. He offers his ten crore Narayana troops to one side and himself, unarmed, to the other, and Arjuna picks Krishna as his charioteer. Duryodhana takes the army and gains an extra force from Kritavarman, while Balarama refuses to fight for either side.

scenes.B05C007S01: Krishna offers his army or himself to the two rivals, Arjuna picks Krishna, Duryodhana takes the troops, and Balarama refuses to fight.
scenes.B05C007S02: Arjuna returns to Yudhishthira with Krishna at his side.

shots.B05C007S01H01: The Pandava and Kaurava messengers are sent out, Arjuna sets off for Dwaraka, and Duryodhana arrives there first with a few troops and waits while Krishna sleeps; Arjuna comes in after him.
shots.B05C007S01H02: Duryodhana asks Krishna for help, and Krishna replies that both came to him and offers his army or himself unarmed, letting Arjuna choose first. Arjuna chooses Krishna, and Duryodhana takes the army. Balarama then declines to fight for either side.
shots.B05C007S01H03: Duryodhana, though he has lost Krishna, is pleased with the army and gains a further army from Kritavarman. Krishna asks Arjuna why he picked a man who will not fight.
shots.B05C007S01H04: Arjuna explains that Krishna is strong enough to win alone, that he wants the fame of having Krishna on his side, and that he has long wished for Krishna to drive his chariot.
shots.B05C007S01H05: Krishna agrees to be Arjuna's charioteer and says the wish will be granted.
shots.B05C007S02H01: Arjuna and Krishna, along with other leaders of the Dasarha clan, return happily to Yudhishthira.

B05C008.summary: The king of the Madras, Salya, marches to join the Pandavas with a large army. Duryodhana secretly arranges lavish hospitality along the way, and Salya is so impressed that he offers a boon. Duryodhana asks him to lead the Kaurava army, and Salya agrees, then goes to visit Yudhishthira. There Yudhishthira asks him to weaken Karna in their future duel, and Salya agrees, though reluctantly, after consoling the Pandavas for their hardships.

scenes.B05C008S01: Salya marches toward the Pandavas, is entertained by Duryodhana, promises to lead the Kauravas, and then visits Yudhishthira, who asks for his help against Karna.

shots.B05C008S01H01: Salya's huge army marches toward the Pandavas, shaking the earth. Duryodhana, hearing of his approach, arranges lavish entertainment along the route, and Salya is so pleased that he asks to reward the men who built it.
shots.B05C008S01H02: Duryodhana, revealed as the host, asks Salya for a boon: that he lead the entire army.
shots.B05C008S01H03: Salya agrees, and the two men part. Salya goes to meet the Pandavas, greets them warmly, and praises Yudhishthira's virtue and the hardships he endured.
shots.B05C008S01H04: Yudhishthira tells Salya about the boon Duryodhana has won. He asks Salya to be Karna's charioteer in the coming duel with Arjuna and to undermine Karna's confidence. Salya agrees to do so, saying that Destiny rules and that even the gods have suffered.

B05C009.summary: Yudhishthira asks how Indra and his wife came to suffer great misery, and Salya tells the old myth in reply. Twashtri creates a three-headed son to rival Indra, and Indra has him tempted and then killed, first with a thunderbolt and then by a carpenter who cuts off his heads. Twashtri creates Vritra to destroy Indra, who is swallowed but escapes, and the gods finally turn to Vishnu for help. The story is told to console Yudhishthira that even gods suffer, and it ends before the Vritra battle is resolved.

scenes.B05C009S01: Yudhishthira asks about Indra's suffering, and Salya tells of the three-headed son, his killing, and the creation of Vritra.

shots.B05C009S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Salya to explain how Indra and his queen came to endure such great misery.
shots.B05C009S01H02: Salya begins the tale: Twashtri, out of hatred for Indra, makes a three-headed son who practices austerities and eyes Indra's throne. Indra, afraid, sends nymphs to tempt him away from his austerities.
shots.B05C009S01H03: The nymphs agree to try to seduce the three-headed son and so ease Indra's fear.
shots.B05C009S01H04: The nymphs fail, since the son's senses are fully under control. Indra then strikes him down with his thunderbolt, and when the body still looks alive, Indra orders a passing carpenter to cut off the heads. The carpenter objects, Indra insists, and promises the carpenter a share of sacrificial offerings.
shots.B05C009S01H05: The carpenter severs the heads, and birds fly out of each mouth. Twashtri, furious, creates Vritra to kill Indra, and a long battle follows in which Vritra swallows Indra. Indra escapes through a yawn, the gods are defeated, and they finally turn to Vishnu for help.

B05C010.summary: Indra admits that Vritra has grown too strong for him, so the gods and sages go to Vishnu for help. Vishnu advises peace and says he will hide inside Indra's thunderbolt. The sages persuade Vritra to accept friendship, and he sets terms meant to keep him from being killed by any ordinary means. Indra kills him at dusk with a froth-covered thunderbolt that Vishnu animates, but Indra then falls into guilt for killing the holy man's son and hides, leaving the world without a king.

scenes.B05C010S01: Indra asks for help against Vritra, the gods go to Vishnu, the sages make peace with Vritra, and Indra kills him by a trick and is then left guilt-stricken and hidden.

shots.B05C010S01H01: Indra tells the gods that Vritra has pervaded the universe and that he himself is no longer able to oppose him, so they must seek Vishnu's help.
shots.B05C010S01H02: The gods and sages praise Vishnu and ask for his help. Vishnu advises them to seek peace with Vritra and says he will enter Indra's thunderbolt to secure victory.
shots.B05C010S01H03: The sages approach Vritra and urge him to make friends with Indra. Vritra replies that friendship between enemies is impossible, and the sages argue that friendship with the righteous is always worth seeking.
shots.B05C010S01H04: Vritra agrees to peace on the condition that he not be killed by any material, weapon, or time of day. Indra later finds him at dusk by the sea and kills him with a mass of froth fused with the thunderbolt, with Vishnu inside it. Indra is then overcome by guilt for killing the holy man's son and hides, and the world is left in disorder and without a king.

B05C011.summary: With Indra gone, the gods and sages make Nahusha king of heaven, and at first he is reluctant and then accepts. Once he holds power, he gives himself over to pleasure and lust. He then demands that Indra's queen Sachi come to his palace, and she takes refuge with the priest Vrihaspati, who promises to reunite her with Indra. Nahusha grows enraged at this refusal.

scenes.B05C011S01: The gods make Nahusha king, he turns to lust, and he is angered when Indra's queen takes refuge with Vrihaspati.

shots.B05C011S01H01: The gods and sages crown Nahusha as king of heaven despite his protests. His power grows, but he turns to indulgence and demands that Sachi come to him. Sachi asks Vrihaspati for protection, and he promises she will be reunited with Indra, which angers Nahusha.

B05C012.summary: The gods try to calm Nahusha, who refuses to give up his demand for Sachi and argues that Indra himself was guilty of similar wrongs. They ask Vrihaspati to hand Sachi over, but he refuses to betray someone who has sought his protection and warns of the ruin that follows such betrayal. The gods then persuade Sachi to ask Nahusha for time, and she agrees to visit him.

scenes.B05C012S01: The gods plead with Nahusha to calm down, Vrihaspati refuses to give Sachi up, and the gods advise her to ask Nahusha for time.
scenes.B05C012S02: The gods persuade Sachi to go to Nahusha, and he is pleased by her beauty.

shots.B05C012S01H01: The gods plead with Nahusha to restrain his anger and give up his designs on another man's wife, but he is blinded by lust and refuses, citing Indra's own past misdeeds.
shots.B05C012S01H02: The gods promise to bring Indra's queen to Nahusha and urge him to calm down.
shots.B05C012S01H03: The gods go to Vrihaspati and ask him to hand Sachi over, and Sachi begs him for protection and deliverance from Nahusha.
shots.B05C012S01H04: Vrihaspati refuses to betray someone who has sought his protection, and he cites a saying of Brahma that anyone who gives up a suppliant will lose protection and be ruined.
shots.B05C012S01H05: The gods ask Vrihaspati for a practical solution, and he advises that Sachi ask Nahusha for time to decide, which will help both her and the gods.
shots.B05C012S02H01: The gods accept this advice, and led by Agni they urge Sachi to go to Nahusha, saying he will soon fall and Indra will regain his rule. Sachi goes to Nahusha, who is pleased by her beauty.

B05C013.summary: Sachi asks Nahusha for time to look for Indra, and he agrees on condition that she come back. The gods turn to Vishnu, who tells Indra to perform a horse sacrifice to cleanse himself of the guilt for killing the holy man's son. Indra performs the rite and passes his guilt on to trees, rivers, mountains, earth and women. Still afraid of Nahusha, Indra vanishes again, and Sachi, grieving, calls on the goddesses Night and Divination to find him.

scenes.B05C013S01: Sachi asks Nahusha for time to find Indra, the gods consult Vishnu, Indra cleanses himself by sacrifice and vanishes again, and Sachi calls on Divination.

shots.B05C013S01H01: Sachi asks Nahusha for time to search for Indra and promises to return. The gods consult Vishnu, who tells Indra to perform a horse sacrifice to cleanse himself. Indra does so, shares out his guilt among the natural world, and still fears Nahusha, so he vanishes again. Sachi grieves and invokes Night and the goddess of Divination.

B05C014.summary: The goddess of Divination guides Sachi north of the Himalayas to a lake, where she finds Indra hidden inside a lotus stalk. Sachi shrinks to his size and praises his past deeds, then tells him about Nahusha's threats. She asks Indra to destroy Nahusha and take back the heavens. The chapter brings Indra and his queen back together, ready to act against the usurper.

scenes.B05C014S01: Divination leads Sachi to the lake where Indra is hidden, and Sachi tells him of Nahusha's threats and asks him to act.

shots.B05C014S01H01: Divination appears to Sachi and offers to lead her to Indra. They journey over mountains and across the sea to a lake, where Sachi finds Indra hidden in a lotus stalk. She describes Nahusha's acts and begs Indra to destroy him and reclaim his throne.

B05C015.summary: Indra's plan is to have Sachi flatter Nahusha into being carried by sages in a palanquin, which Nahusha accepts. Sachi begs Vrihaspati to find Indra quickly, and Vrihaspati sends Agni, the fire god, to search for him. Agni searches the land and sky but refuses to enter the waters, saying water would extinguish him. The chapter shows the search for Indra stalled before its turning point.

scenes.B05C015S01: Indra's plan to have Nahusha carried by sages is carried out, and Vrihaspati sends Agni to search for Indra.
scenes.B05C015S02: Agni refuses to enter the waters, saying water would put him out.

shots.B05C015S01H01: Indra tells Sachi that force will not work against Nahusha and asks her to secretly tell Nahusha that he will yield if carried in a vehicle borne by sages.
shots.B05C015S01H02: Sachi goes to Nahusha, who welcomes her warmly and swears to do as she asks. She then makes her request for a vehicle carried by sages, which Indra has never had before.
shots.B05C015S01H03: Nahusha is flattered, agrees, and boasts of his power, saying the seven sages and other holy men will carry him.
shots.B05C015S01H04: Nahusha harnesses sages to his car, treats them with contempt, and drives them. Sachi goes to Vrihaspati, saying her time is nearly up, and asks him to find Indra quickly.
shots.B05C015S01H05: Vrihaspati reassures Sachi that Nahusha will soon fall. He makes a fire offering and asks Agni to search for Indra. Agni searches everywhere on land and sky, returns, and says the waters are the only place left, which he does not want to enter.
shots.B05C015S02H01: Agni protests that entering water would mean his extinction, and he leaves himself in Vrihaspati's hands. He notes that the sources of the things that conquer others are not overcome by them.

B05C016.summary: Vrihaspati praises Agni at length, and Agni agrees to enter the waters and find Indra. Agni finds Indra hidden in a lotus stalk, and Vrihaspati praises Indra's past victories and urges him to act. Indra asks how Nahusha rose, and Vrihaspati explains that the gods had made him king and that he now terrorizes the worlds. Other guardian gods then offer their help against Nahusha in return for shares of sacrifice, and Indra allots them domains.

scenes.B05C016S01: Agni finds Indra in the lotus, and Vrihaspati explains to Indra how Nahusha came to power.
scenes.B05C016S02: The guardian gods agree to help Indra, who rewards them with domains and shares of sacrifice.

shots.B05C016S01H01: Vrihaspati praises Agni as the mouth of the gods and carrier of offerings, and Agni agrees to enter the waters to find Indra.
shots.B05C016S01H02: Agni finds Indra inside a lotus stalk and reports back. Vrihaspati and the gods go to Indra and praise his past victories, urging him to rise and act once more.
shots.B05C016S01H03: Vrihaspati tells Indra that the human king Nahusha, given the throne by the sages, is causing great trouble.
shots.B05C016S01H04: Indra asks how Nahusha got the throne and what austerities earned him such power.
shots.B05C016S01H05: Vrihaspati explains that the gods, frightened after Indra left, made Nahusha king by giving him their power. Now Nahusha is terrifying, uses the sages to carry him, and his gaze can drain others' strength, so the gods hide from him.
shots.B05C016S02H01: The guardian gods, Kuvera, Yama, Soma and Varuna, arrive and congratulate Indra. They say they fear Nahusha and agree to help if Indra defeats him and they keep their shares of sacrifice. Agni asks for a share too, and Indra agrees.
shots.B05C016S02H02: Indra rewards the guardians, giving Kuvera rule over the Yakshas and wealth, Yama rule over the ancestors, and Varuna rule over the waters.

B05C017.summary: The sage Agastya visits Indra while the gods are planning how to defeat Nahusha. Indra asks how Nahusha fell, and Agastya explains that the proud king mocked the sacred hymns, insulted the sages carrying him, and kicked Agastya on the head. Agastya cursed him to roam the earth as a huge snake for ten thousand years. The gods and all the other beings rejoice at Nahusha's fall.

scenes.B05C017S01: Agastya greets Indra, tells how Nahusha was cursed for his insults, and the gods and other beings rejoice.

shots.B05C017S01H01: The sage Agastya arrives while Indra is planning against Nahusha and congratulates Indra on surviving the death of Vritra and the son of Twashtri, and on Nahusha's fall.
shots.B05C017S01H02: Indra welcomes Agastya and offers him the customary water, seat and cow.
shots.B05C017S01H03: Indra asks Agastya to tell how Nahusha was thrown from heaven.
shots.B05C017S01H04: Agastya tells how the sages carrying Nahusha asked whether certain Vedic hymns were valid. Nahusha, blinded by pride, declared them false and kicked Agastya on the head, and Agastya cursed him to become a huge snake for ten thousand years.
shots.B05C017S01H05: The gods, sages, spirits and even the rivers and seas rejoice at Nahusha's downfall and at Indra's survival.

B05C018.summary: Indra returns to the three worlds, riding his elephant, reunited with Sachi and honored by the gods and sages, and he rules well. Salya then tells Yudhishthira that Indra's story shows a fallen rival can be overthrown and that the Pandavas will regain their kingdom in the same way. He predicts that Karna and Duryodhana will also be destroyed and says that hearing the tale brings victory. Yudhishthira asks Salya to undermine Karna by praising Arjuna, and Salya agrees and departs to join Duryodhana.

scenes.B05C018S01: Indra returns to power, Salya encourages Yudhishthira with Indra's story, and Salya agrees to undermine Karna before leaving for Duryodhana.

shots.B05C018S01H01: Indra returns to the three worlds on his elephant, with the gods, Agni, Yama and the others, and is reunited with Sachi. He honors the sage Angiras, rules well, and Salya tells Yudhishthira that he too will regain his kingdom, while Karna and Duryodhana will fall, and that the tale brings victory to its listeners.
shots.B05C018S01H02: Yudhishthira thanks Salya and asks him to serve as Karna's charioteer and damp his spirit by praising Arjuna.
shots.B05C018S01H03: Salya agrees to do as Yudhishthira asks and to help in any other way he can.
shots.B05C018S01H04: Salya takes leave of the Pandavas and marches with his army to Duryodhana.

B05C019.summary: The chapter lists the armies that gather for the two sides. The Pandavas gather seven akshauhinis, which are large army divisions, from many allied kings. Duryodhana gathers eleven akshauhinis from his own allies, which fill the land around Hastinapura so that the city cannot hold them. The Pandava priest sent to the Kauravas sees how huge the Kaurava force has become.

scenes.B05C019S01: The armies of the Pandavas and Kauravas gather, and the Kaurava forces spread across the land around Hastinapura.

shots.B05C019S01H01: The armies gather: Yuyudhana, Dhrishtaketu, Jayatsena, Drupada, Virata, and many other kings join the Pandavas. Bhagadatta, Salya, Bhurishravas, Kritavarman, Jayadratha, and many others join Duryodhana, and the Kaurava force grows to eleven akshauhinis, too large for Hastinapura, so it spreads across the surrounding regions, where the Pandava priest sees it.

B05C020.summary: Drupada's priest, now at Hastinapura, addresses the Kaurava leaders. He argues that the Pandavas have a rightful claim to half of their shared inheritance, that they were robbed and humiliated, and that they now want only a peaceful settlement. He points to the strength of the Pandava army and their allies, and urges the Kauravas to return what is due before it is too late.

scenes.B05C020S01: Drupada's priest, received at the Kaurava court, argues that the Pandavas have a right to their inheritance and asks for peace.

shots.B05C020S01H01: The priest greets Dhritarashtra, Bhishma and Vidura, and asks after the Kauravas before stating the Pandavas' case. He recounts their plunder at dice, their exile and humiliation, and says they desire peace and would rather not destroy the world. He notes their army of seven akshauhinis and the allies that match the Kauravas, and asks the Kauravas to give back what is due.

B05C021.summary: Bhishma receives the priest courteously and agrees that the Pandavas have a legal claim, while praising Arjuna as unbeatable. Karna cuts in with a harsh reply, mocking the Pandavas and insisting that Duryodhana will not give up any land out of fear. Bhishma rebukes Karna, and Dhritarashtra settles the matter by sending Sanjaya to the Pandavas as his envoy.

scenes.B05C021S01: Bhishma and Karna answer the priest, Bhishma rebukes Karna, and Dhritarashtra decides to send Sanjaya to the Pandavas.

shots.B05C021S01H01: Bhishma welcomes the priest's words, grants the Pandavas their claim, and praises Arjuna's skill. Karna interrupts with insults, recalls the dice match and the exile, and says the Pandavas must accept their place or face war.
shots.B05C021S01H02: Bhishma tells Karna that his talk is idle and reminds him how Arjuna once beat six warriors alone, and that the Kauravas will be destroyed if they do not follow the priest's advice.
shots.B05C021S01H03: Dhritarashtra calms Bhishma, rebukes Karna, and says he will send Sanjaya to the Pandavas. He honors the priest and sends him back, and then calls Sanjaya to the council.

B05C022.summary: Dhritarashtra instructs Sanjaya to go to the Pandavas at Upaplavya and greet them warmly. He praises the Pandavas' conduct and blames only Duryodhana and Karna for the hostility. Then he lists the Pandava allies and their formidable warriors, admits that he fears Arjuna and Krishna, and especially fears Yudhishthira's anger. He tells Sanjaya to say that he desires peace, but not in words that will provoke war.

scenes.B05C022S01: Dhritarashtra tells Sanjaya how to greet the Pandavas, praises them, lists their allies, and expresses fear of their anger.

shots.B05C022S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to go to Upaplavya and greet the Pandavas, praising their virtue, blaming Duryodhana and Karna for the hatred, and listing the Pandava champions, including Arjuna, Bhima, the twins, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, Pandya, and the Kekaya princes, whose strength he fears. He admits he fears Yudhishthira's wrath, and asks Sanjaya to visit Krishna and say that Dhritarashtra wants peace, without saying anything that might provoke war.

B05C023.summary: Sanjaya arrives at Upaplavya and greets Yudhishthira warmly, asking after the Pandavas and Draupadi. Yudhishthira responds by asking after the Kaurava elders, the Brahmins, and the women of the household. He then recalls the Pandava feats of arms and asks whether the Kauravas still remember them. He concludes that peace is hard to reach while Duryodhana stays hostile.

scenes.B05C023S01: Sanjaya greets Yudhishthira, who asks after the Kaurava household and reminds the Kauravas of the Pandavas' feats, concluding that peace is hard to reach.

shots.B05C023S01H01: Sanjaya greets Yudhishthira and asks after his health, the health of his brothers, and Draupadi and her sons, and says that Dhritarashtra has inquired after them.
shots.B05C023S01H02: Yudhishthira returns the greetings and asks after Dhritarashtra, Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Karna, and the women and servants of the household, and whether Brahmins still receive their gifts. He then asks whether the Kauravas remember Arjuna's archery, Bhima's strength, the twins' bravery, and their rescue at Dwaitavana, and concludes that peace cannot be reached while Duryodhana stands in the way.

B05C024.summary: Sanjaya replies that the Kaurava leaders are well, though some of their advisers are wicked. He says that Dhritarashtra himself does not approve of the injustice done to the Pandavas and grieves over it, and that he knows internal strife is a great sin. He praises the Pandava heroes, says that the future cannot be known, and asks Yudhishthira to act with wisdom so that peace is restored. Then he prepares to deliver Dhritarashtra's own message.

scenes.B05C024S01: Sanjaya tells Yudhishthira that Dhritarashtra regrets the Pandavas' treatment, praises their heroes, and asks Yudhishthira to hear Dhritarashtra's message.

shots.B05C024S01H01: Sanjaya tells Yudhishthira that the Kauravas are well and that Dhritarashtra regrets the injustice, since he knows that causing internal strife is a great sin. He praises the Pandava heroes, notes that the future is hidden, and asks Yudhishthira to seek a peace that satisfies everyone. He then says he will pass on Dhritarashtra's counsel.

B05C025.summary: Yudhishthira asks Sanjaya to report Dhritarashtra's message to the assembled allies. Sanjaya greets the Pandava leaders, says that Dhritarashtra eagerly welcomes peace, and urges the Pandavas to accept it. He argues that a war would destroy the family, that victory and defeat would be equally empty, and that the Kaurava side is too strong to beat. He ends by asking the Pandavas to keep their ties to the Kurus, which the king and Bhishma also desire.

scenes.B05C025S01: Yudhishthira asks for Dhritarashtra's message, and Sanjaya pleads for peace, arguing that war would bring ruin on both sides.

shots.B05C025S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Sanjaya to gather the allied leaders and tell them what Dhritarashtra has sent him to say.
shots.B05C025S01H02: Sanjaya greets the Pandava leaders and their allies, says that Dhritarashtra welcomes peace, and praises the Pandavas' virtue while warning that a war would destroy their family and cannot be justified by its outcome. He notes the strength of the Kaurava side and asks the Pandavas to yield to peace, a wish that Bhishma and Dhritarashtra also share.

B05C026.summary: Yudhishthira replies that he would much prefer peace to war, but he refuses to be humiliated. He blames Dhritarashtra for listening to his wicked son Duryodhana and sending away the wise Vidura, and he names Dussasana, Sakuni and Karna as Duryodhana's advisers. He says the Kauravas underestimate Arjuna and the Pandava brothers, and he is willing to forgive if the Kauravas return at least the land of Indraprastha. The speech shows his willingness to compromise, though he holds firm on his share.

scenes.B05C026S01: Yudhishthira prefers peace, blames Dhritarashtra and Duryodhana for the crisis, and asks only for Indraprastha as his share.

shots.B05C026S01H01: Yudhishthira says that peace is better than war and that the Pandavas seek only the happiness that comes from righteousness. He describes the comforts that Dhritarashtra enjoys and says the king has followed his wicked son against the advice of Vidura. He names Duryodhana's counselors and argues that the Kauravas are wrong to think they can keep the kingdom while the Pandava warriors are alive, though he would forgive them and asks for Indraprastha as his share.

B05C027.summary: Sanjaya urges Yudhishthira to give up the war, arguing that a good name is worth more than kingdoms and that begging among his kinsmen would be better than winning by slaughter. He warns that desire, greed and wrath lead to sin, that virtue is the only path to lasting reward, and that the Pandavas had many chances to strike earlier and did not. He says that Bhishma, Drona and the other elders would all fall in the fighting. He ends by urging Yudhishthira to yield, saying that giving everything up is better than the path of war.

scenes.B05C027S01: Sanjaya urges Yudhishthira to give up war, arguing that virtue, a good name and the lives of the elders matter more than the kingdom.

shots.B05C027S01H01: Sanjaya urges Yudhishthira to avoid war, arguing that a good name matters more than a kingdom and that living on alms would be better than winning by war. He argues that desire and greed bind people and that virtue is what counts, and he reminds Yudhishthira of his past holy life, of the rites and gifts he has made, and of the cost of war to the elders. He says the Pandavas could have struck earlier, questions why they now choose war, calls wrath a poison, and tells Yudhishthira to yield, saying that giving everything up is better than the path to war.

B05C028.summary: Yudhishthira answers that righteous conduct is the highest good but that dharma depends on circumstances, and that duties can shift in times of distress. He says that the Pandavas will not seek wealth by unrighteous means, not even the realms of the gods. He calls on Krishna to judge whether his refusal to accept peace or his decision to fight is justified, and he points to the strength of his allies, who follow Krishna's counsel. He closes by saying he always respects Krishna's views.

scenes.B05C028S01: Yudhishthira argues that duty can shift in hard times and asks Krishna to judge whether he is right to refuse the terms and fight.

shots.B05C028S01H01: Yudhishthira agrees that virtue is the highest course but argues that right and wrong can be hard to tell apart, and that duties shift in times of distress. He says he will not gain even heaven by unrighteous means. He asks Krishna, who is wise and well informed, to say whether the Pandavas would be blameworthy for refusing peace and fighting instead, and he notes that his allies follow Krishna's counsel and that he always defers to Krishna.

B05C029.summary: Krishna answers Sanjaya's appeal for peace by defending Yudhishthira's readiness to act and arguing that action, not inaction, brings reward. He points to the gods and sages, who gained their places through disciplined work, and he sets out the duties of each class, saying a king must punish wrongdoers and that Dhritarashtra's seizure of the Pandava share is unlawful. He recalls the insults at the dice game and the humiliation of Draupadi in the council hall. He says he will go to the Kauravas himself to try for peace, but warns that the Kauravas will be destroyed if they refuse.

scenes.B05C029S01: Krishna defends the Pandavas' right to act, recalls the Kaurava wrongs, and says he will go to Hastinapura himself to seek peace.

shots.B05C029S01H01: Krishna's long reply: he wants peace for both families, defends the Pandavas' conduct as lawful, argues that work brings rewards as seen in the gods, sages and the rest of the world, and sets out the duties of each caste. He says the king must punish wrongdoers, that Dhritarashtra has unlawfully seized the Pandava share, and recalls how Draupadi was humiliated and how the Kauravas and Karna stood by. He concludes that he will go to the Kauravas to seek peace, warning that they will be destroyed by the Pandavas if they refuse.

B05C030.summary: Sanjaya takes his leave of Yudhishthira, who praises him for his honest and loyal service as envoy. Yudhishthira then gives him a long list of people to greet in Hastinapura, from Brahmins and the elders to the women, servants, and allied kings. He asks Sanjaya to bring a final message to Duryodhana: return Indraprastha or fight. The chapter closes Sanjaya's mission and leaves the choice of peace or war with the Kauravas.

scenes.B05C030S01: Sanjaya takes his leave, Yudhishthira praises him and sends greetings to a long list of Kaurava figures, and the final demand goes to Duryodhana.

shots.B05C030S01H01: Sanjaya takes leave of Yudhishthira and of Krishna, Bhima, Arjuna, the twins, Satyaki and Chekitana, asking that all the kings look on him kindly.
shots.B05C030S01H02: Yudhishthira praises Sanjaya as an honest and trusted envoy and sends him off with greetings for the Brahmins, Drona, Ashvatthama, Kripa, Bhishma, Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana, Dussasana, the kings who have joined the Kauravas, the women, servants and others. He ends by telling Sanjaya to tell Duryodhana to return Indraprastha or fight.

B05C031.summary: Yudhishthira gives Sanjaya his final message for Dhritarashtra. He reminds the old king that the kingdom was given to the Pandavas through his grace, asks him to keep the family together, and urges him not to be indifferent to them. He asks Duryodhana to forgive the injuries done to the Pandavas and to give them five villages, which would end the quarrel. He says he is capable of both war and peace, and the choice rests with the Kauravas.

scenes.B05C031S01: Yudhishthira sends Sanjaya back with a final message to Dhritarashtra, Bhishma, Vidura and Duryodhana, asking for peace on modest terms.

shots.B05C031S01H01: Yudhishthira's long message: he tells Sanjaya to speak to the Kaurava elders, asks Dhritarashtra to keep the family together, requests a share of the kingdom from Duryodhana, offers peace for five villages, and says that he is ready for either peace or war.

B05C032.summary: Sanjaya returns to Hastinapura and is admitted to Dhritarashtra's chamber. He passes on Yudhishthira's greetings and the Pandava good wishes, and Dhritarashtra asks after Yudhishthira's family and counselors. Sanjaya then answers with a blunt rebuke, saying that Yudhishthira is virtuous while Dhritarashtra's unjust policy will bring ruin on the family. He asks leave to rest before reporting to the full council the next morning.

scenes.B05C032S01: Sanjaya reports to Dhritarashtra, passes on Yudhishthira's greetings, then rebukes the king for his unjust policy and asks to be excused until morning.

shots.B05C032S01H01: Sanjaya reaches Hastinapura and asks the gatekeeper to tell Dhritarashtra that he has arrived from the Pandavas, and the gatekeeper goes to inform the king.
shots.B05C032S01H02: Dhritarashtra tells the gatekeeper to admit Sanjaya at once.
shots.B05C032S01H03: Sanjaya enters the chamber, bows to Dhritarashtra, and passes on Yudhishthira's greetings and his enquiry after the king's sons and counselors.
shots.B05C032S01H04: Dhritarashtra blesses Yudhishthira and asks whether he is well with his brothers and counselors.
shots.B05C032S01H05: Sanjaya replies that Yudhishthira is well and virtuous, and that he cares for justice above wealth. He tells Dhritarashtra that his own unjust conduct is shameful and will bring misery on the family, notes that the counselors are determined not to restore the Pandava share, and warns that Arjuna will burn the Kurus. He ends by asking leave to rest, since the council will hear Yudhishthira's message the next morning.

B05C033.summary: Dhritarashtra, anxious after Sanjaya's blunt report and unsure what Yudhishthira's message will be, sends for Vidura. Vidura notes that Yudhishthira was wronged, that the blind king had no claim to the throne, and that the kingdom has been placed in the hands of Duryodhana, Shakuni, Karna and Dussasana. He then gives a long discourse on the marks of wisdom and folly, the value of forgiveness, and the dangers of greed and pride, and he urges the king to return the Pandavas' share of the kingdom.

scenes.B05C033S01: Dhritarashtra summons Vidura, who reproaches him for wronging the Pandavas and then gives a long discourse on wisdom, folly and forgiveness, urging him to return their share.

shots.B05C033S01H01: Dhritarashtra sends for Vidura, and the attendant brings Vidura in to the inner chamber, where the king says he is always ready to see him.
shots.B05C033S01H02: Vidura enters with joined hands and offers to do whatever the king needs.
shots.B05C033S01H03: Dhritarashtra admits that Sanjaya has returned and rebuked him, that he does not know Yudhishthira's message, and that his worry has left him burning and unable to sleep.
shots.B05C033S01H04: Vidura says that sleeplessness afflicts thieves, the lustful, the ruined and the weak, and asks whether the king is himself grieving over the wealth of others.
shots.B05C033S01H05: Vidura gives a long discourse on the marks of wise and foolish people, the power of forgiveness, the dangers of pride, greed and anger, and proper conduct for kings. He points out the wrongs done to Yudhishthira and urges the king to return the Pandavas' share of the kingdom, which would bring him credit with gods and men.

B05C034.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura for counsel, since he cannot sleep and fears what Yudhishthira intends. Vidura says he must speak frankly even if the message is unwelcome, and he warns against unjust aims and unrestrained senses. He explains how anger, desire, and cruel speech bring a king to ruin, and that the king's sons have been blinded by their hostility to the Pandavas. He urges Dhritarashtra to let Yudhishthira, who has borne great suffering to protect the king's reputation, rule the kingdom.

scenes.B05C034S01: Dhritarashtra asks for advice, and Vidura warns against unjust aims and unchecked senses and urges him to let Yudhishthira rule.

shots.B05C034S01H01: Dhritarashtra admits he is sleepless and anxious and asks Vidura to advise him on what would be good for Yudhishthira and for the Kurus.
shots.B05C034S01H02: Vidura says he will speak truthfully, warns against unjust aims, and sets out the marks of a wise king: he must know his own strength, control his senses, and avoid evil counsel. He says the tongue can wound more deeply than any weapon, that the blindness of his sons has clouded their minds, and that Yudhishthira deserves to rule the earth.

B05C035.summary: Dhritarashtra asks for more of Vidura's teaching. Vidura tells the tale of Virochana and Sudhanwan, who wager their lives in a dispute over a seat and then take the question to Prahlada. Prahlada rules that Sudhanwan is the superior and that he, though his own son is at stake, will not lie. Vidura draws from this that a ruler should never lie for land, that false speech brings ruin, and that virtue and good conduct are the only lasting foundation of fortune. He ends by urging the king to trust the Pandavas and to see them as his own sons.

scenes.B05C035S01: Vidura tells the story of Virochana and Sudhanwan and Prahlada's judgment, then teaches that a lie for land brings ruin.
scenes.B05C035S02: Vidura gives a further list of virtues, vices and good conduct, and ends by urging Dhritarashtra to trust the Pandavas.

shots.B05C035S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks for more of Vidura's teaching, saying he has not had enough.
shots.B05C035S01H02: Vidura begins a tale in which the maiden Kesini must choose between the Asura Virochana and the Brahmin Sudhanwan, and Virochana boasts that the Asuras are the best of creatures.
shots.B05C035S01H03: Sudhanwan refuses to sit as Virochana's equal, and the two agree to wager their lives on the question of which is superior, taking the matter to Prahlada.
shots.B05C035S01H04: Prahlada declares that Sudhanwan is the superior and that Virochana has lost. He explains that a lie told for gain, whether for cattle, horses or land, brings ruin on one's ancestors and family, and he refuses to lie even to save his son. Sudhanwan spares Virochana's life on condition that he wash the feet of Kesini.
shots.B05C035S01H05: Vidura concludes that a king should never lie for land, that the gods help those who value righteousness, and that the Vedas abandon the deceitful. He lists the sinful acts to avoid, the kinds of people who cannot testify, and the ways character is tested by hardship, and says that a king who favors a person can help that person shine with the eight marks of good character.
shots.B05C035S02H01: Vidura lists the paths of righteousness, the marks of the wise and the foolish, and the ways to act across each day and season of life. He warns that wrongful wealth leaves gaps, that a sinful person is punished for sin, and he ends by urging Dhritarashtra to trust the Pandavas, who depend on him as their father, and not to rely on Duryodhana, Sakuni, Dussasana and Karna.

B05C036.summary: Vidura tells the tale of the sage son of Atri, who teaches the Sadhyas to bear insults patiently, avoid harsh speech, and keep good company. Dhritarashtra then asks what makes a family noble, and Vidura answers that good conduct and disciplined religious life matter more than wealth, and that quarrels and disrespect to Brahmins bring families down. Dhritarashtra admits he has deceived Yudhishthira and fears destruction, and Vidura urges him to restrain greed and anger, make peace with the Pandavas, and stop Duryodhana. The advice is the last part of Vidura's counsel before the king is pressed toward the council.

scenes.B05C036S01: Vidura tells the sage's tale, explains what makes a family noble, and urges Dhritarashtra to restrain his greed and make peace with the Pandavas.

shots.B05C036S01H01: Vidura tells the tale of the sage son of Atri, who teaches the Sadhyas that patience, restraint and avoiding harsh speech and bad company lead to virtue, and that the slanderer carries the sin of his words.
shots.B05C036S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura what makes a family high.
shots.B05C036S01H03: Vidura says that noble families are marked by asceticism, self-control, study of the Vedas, sacrifice, proper marriage and generosity, and that they decline through quarrels, disrespect to Brahmins and dishonesty. He notes that good conduct matters more than wealth, that true friends are tested by need, and that grief and restless passions weaken a person.
shots.B05C036S01H04: Dhritarashtra admits that he has deceived Yudhishthira and fears that the Pandavas will destroy his sons, and he asks Vidura for words to calm his anxiety.
shots.B05C036S01H05: Vidura urges the king to seek knowledge and self-control and to give up greed, notes that kinsmen are strong when they stay together, and asks him to make peace with the Pandavas and restrain Duryodhana, since strength combined with gentleness brings lasting prosperity.

B05C037.summary: Vidura lists the kinds of foolish people whose efforts are wasted, then answers Dhritarashtra's question about why people do not live to a hundred by naming six vices that cut life short. He warns that the Kaurava policy is folly, since the king has favored his lesser sons over the Pandavas, and he gives long advice on how a king should treat servants, counselors, and his own household. He presses again for peace, arguing that a rupture with the Pandavas would shame the Kurus and bring ruin, and he closes by praising wisdom as the highest strength.

scenes.B05C037S01: Vidura lists foolish conduct and the vices that shorten life, then gives long advice on servants, counselors and household conduct.
scenes.B05C037S02: Vidura warns against a rupture with the Pandavas and names the five kinds of strength, with intellect the greatest.

shots.B05C037S01H01: Vidura lists the seventeen kinds of foolish people, such as those who try to control the uncontrollable or ask for gifts they should not ask for, and notes that Yama's messengers drag them to hell.
shots.B05C037S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks why, if the Vedas give a hundred years of life, people often do not reach that span.
shots.B05C037S01H03: Vidura says that excess pride, talk, eating, anger, pleasure and quarrels are the six swords that cut life short.
shots.B05C037S01H04: Vidura lists the sins equal to killing a Brahmin and the qualities that lead to heaven, such as gratitude, truthfulness and generosity.
shots.B05C037S01H05: Vidura gives long advice: frank counsel is rare and valuable, wealth and family are to be used for protection, gambling leads to quarrels, the king has preferred jackals to lions, and a king should treat his servants and counselors fairly and choose his men with care.
shots.B05C037S02H01: Vidura warns that a break with the Pandavas would bring enmity among the sons, endless anxiety, shame on the Kurus, and joy to their enemies. He again uses the image of the forest and the tigers to plead that the family must be kept together.
shots.B05C037S02H02: Vidura lists five kinds of strength, placing the strength of intellect above arms, counselors, wealth and birth, and warns against trusting the untrustworthy.

B05C038.summary: Vidura continues his counsel with rules for hospitality, household management, and the handling of secrets. He tells the king which kinds of people to honor and which to shun, how to guard wives and the household, and how a king should choose and test ministers. He stresses patience, careful planning, and restraint in anger and quarrels. He ends by warning that the king has placed power in Duryodhana's hands and cast away the Pandavas, so his fortune will fade like that of Bali.

scenes.B05C038S01: Vidura gives rules on guests, household, secrets and ministers, and warns Dhritarashtra that he has handed power to Duryodhana and cast off the Pandavas.

shots.B05C038S01H01: Vidura gives long rules on receiving guests, on who should not be welcomed, on guarding wives and the household, on keeping state secrets, choosing ministers, managing enemies, and avoiding pointless quarrels, and he ends by warning that Dhritarashtra's prosperity will fall as Bali's did after he cast off the Pandavas and gave power to Duryodhana.

B05C039.summary: Dhritarashtra says that people are moved by destiny like puppets, and Vidura replies with maxims on friendship, kinship and good conduct. Vidura again urges that Duryodhana should have been cast off at birth and that the king should protect his relatives, especially the Pandavas, and undo the wrongs done to them. Dhritarashtra admits the force of this advice but says he cannot abandon his son. The chapter sets the old king's weakness against Vidura's steady counsel.

scenes.B05C039S01: Dhritarashtra says that destiny rules men, and Vidura gives long counsel on abandoning Duryodhana and protecting the Pandavas, which Dhritarashtra refuses.

shots.B05C039S01H01: Dhritarashtra says that man does not control his fortune and is like a wooden doll moved by strings, since the Creator placed him under destiny, and he asks Vidura to continue.
shots.B05C039S01H02: Vidura gives maxims on pleasing others and on sound judgment, then says that Duryodhana should have been abandoned at birth, since the loss of one son would have secured the hundred.
shots.B05C039S01H03: Dhritarashtra says that Vidura's advice is wise but that he cannot abandon his son, and he adds that where there is righteousness there is victory.
shots.B05C039S01H04: Vidura urges the king to help poor relatives, to give the Pandavas a few villages, to undo the wrongs Duryodhana has done, and to keep his family together. He adds long maxims on friendship, forgiveness, perseverance, and the dangers of envy and pride.

B05C040.summary: Vidura continues with teaching on the virtues and vices of students and rulers, the value of forgiveness, and the lasting nature of righteousness compared with fleeting pleasure. He describes the duties of each class and says that Yudhishthira is in danger of falling from the duties of a Kshatriya, so Dhritarashtra should restore him to the throne. Dhritarashtra admits that his mind leans toward the Pandavas but that Duryodhana turns him away, and he concludes that destiny cannot be resisted.

scenes.B05C040S01: Vidura gives a long moral discourse urging Dhritarashtra to restore Yudhishthira, and Dhritarashtra admits he is pulled toward Duryodhana and says destiny rules.

shots.B05C040S01H01: Vidura gives a long discourse on pride and modesty, the faults of students and rulers, the dangers of envy and greed, the lasting value of virtue, the soul as a river, the duties of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras, and finally urges that Yudhishthira be restored to the duties of a king.
shots.B05C040S01H02: Dhritarashtra says he agrees with Vidura and inclines toward the Pandavas, but that his mind turns away when he meets Duryodhana, and he concludes that destiny cannot be averted.

B05C041.summary: Vidura says he has said all he can, since he was born a Sudra, and that the sage Sanatsujata, who teaches that there is no death, can settle Dhritarashtra's doubts. Dhritarashtra asks how he might meet the sage, and Vidura summons him. The sage is then asked to explain the doubts that trouble the king. The section marks a turn toward a more philosophical teaching.

scenes.B05C041S01: Vidura says he cannot teach further and names the sage Sanatsujata as the better teacher for Dhritarashtra's doubts.
scenes.B05C041S02: Dhritarashtra asks how to meet the sage, and Vidura summons him to explain the king's doubts.

shots.B05C041S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura to say whatever remains unsaid, since he finds the discourse charming.
shots.B05C041S01H03: Vidura names the ancient sage Sanatsujata, who has taught that there is no death, and says he can resolve all of the king's doubts.
shots.B05C041S01H04: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura to give the teaching himself, if he has the wisdom.
shots.B05C041S01H05: Vidura declines, saying he was born a Sudra and so should not go further, but he praises the sage's wisdom.
shots.B05C041S02H01: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura how he might meet the ancient sage in his present body.
shots.B05C041S02H02: Vaisampayana reports that Vidura calls the sage, who appears. Vidura asks him to explain Dhritarashtra's doubts so that the king can bear loss, gain, sorrow, age and death.

B05C042.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanatsujata whether death can be avoided or whether there is no death at all. The sage answers that ignorance is death and knowledge is immortality, and that desire, lust and anger are the path to death, while those who conquer their desires are beyond its reach. Dhritarashtra then asks whether ritual action can free a person, and Sanatsujata says that knowledge and renunciation lead more surely to liberation than ritual, while those who show off their learning gain nothing. The teaching shifts the question of salvation from ritual to inner knowledge.

scenes.B05C042S01: Dhritarashtra asks whether death can be avoided, and Sanatsujata explains that ignorance is death and that knowledge and self-control are the way to immortality.
scenes.B05C042S02: Dhritarashtra asks whether ritual or renunciation brings liberation, and Sanatsujata teaches that knowledge is superior and that true Brahmins do not display their learning.

shots.B05C042S01H01: Dhritarashtra, having praised Vidura's words, asks Sanatsujata in private whether there is death, since he has heard that the gods and Asuras practise austerities to avoid it.
shots.B05C042S01H02: Sanatsujata says both views are true: death comes from ignorance, and knowledge brings immortality. He shows how desire, lust and anger lead men to death, while self-control and knowledge free them from it.
shots.B05C042S01H03: Dhritarashtra asks why a learned person should not still practise rituals, since the Vedas promise liberation to those who perform them.
shots.B05C042S01H04: Sanatsujata replies that those who do not know the truth may reach heaven by ritual, but a person who gives up desire and knows the Self attains liberation at once, while ritual alone requires a path that must be kept free of return.
shots.B05C042S01H05: Dhritarashtra asks who the unborn and ancient one is, and how such a being, which pervades all things, can act or feel happiness.
shots.B05C042S02H01: Sanatsujata says the Supreme Soul is the one reality, that the universe springs from it through transformations, and that the Vedas affirm this power of self-transformation.
shots.B05C042S02H02: Dhritarashtra asks whether virtue can overcome vice, or whether virtue can itself be destroyed by vice.
shots.B05C042S02H03: Sanatsujata says both virtue and inaction lead to liberation, but the wise person succeeds through knowledge while the person of action gains merit and must work to remove sin.
shots.B05C042S02H04: Dhritarashtra asks for the ranks of the eternal worlds reached by virtuous Brahmins, and for descriptions of other worlds too, saying he does not want to hear about sinful acts.
shots.B05C042S02H05: Sanatsujata describes the regions reached by different kinds of Brahmins: those who take pride in yoga go to Brahman, those devoted to sacrifice go to the gods, and the learned man who hides his superiority is praised. Those who display their learning to earn food are condemned, and only the one who knows the Supreme and is humble is truly honored.

B05C043.summary: Dhritarashtra asks what silence (mauna) means and whether learning can bring liberation, and Sanatsujata explains that the Supreme Soul is silent because the Vedas and mind cannot grasp it. He says that the Vedas do not free a person whose senses are unrestrained or who lives by deceit, and he describes the faults that spoil asceticism along with the forms of renunciation and self-knowledge. He stresses truth as the foundation of all religious life. The chapter closes with Sanatsujata's teaching that the Brahman is one, that it is found within oneself, and that reading alone does not make a true Brahmin.

scenes.B05C043S01: Dhritarashtra asks about silence and whether the Vedas free a person who sins, and Sanatsujata says that unrestrained living cannot be saved by the Vedas alone.
scenes.B05C043S02: Sanatsujata explains that asceticism is successful when it is free from faults, and he lists the faults that spoil it.
scenes.B05C043S03: Sanatsujata explains the six kinds of renunciation, the virtues of self-restraint and self-knowledge, and that there is one Brahman, known within oneself.

shots.B05C043S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks what silence means, which kind of silence Sanatsujata prefers, and whether a learned man can reach liberation through it.
shots.B05C043S01H02: Sanatsujata says the Supreme Soul cannot be grasped by the Vedas or by the mind, and so it is called silent, and that it is the source of the sacred syllable Om and of ordinary speech.
shots.B05C043S01H03: Dhritarashtra asks whether a man who knows the Vedas remains tainted when he commits sin.
shots.B05C043S01H04: Sanatsujata says that a person who has not restrained his senses is not saved by any Veda, and that the Vedas abandon the deceitful as young birds leave their nest.
shots.B05C043S01H05: Dhritarashtra asks why Brahmins still claim that the Vedas destroy sin if they cannot save a person without virtue.
shots.B05C043S02H01: Sanatsujata says the universe springs from the Supreme Soul through conditions, that asceticism and sacrifice lead toward it, and that those who only seek worldly fruits must return to the cycle of action.
shots.B05C043S02H02: Dhritarashtra asks why asceticism sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails.
shots.B05C043S02H03: Sanatsujata says that asceticism free from faults leads to liberation, while asceticism spoiled by vanity and lack of true devotion fails.
shots.B05C043S02H04: Dhritarashtra asks for an account of the faults that spoil asceticism.
shots.B05C043S02H05: Sanatsujata lists the faults of human beings, including anger, lust, greed, cruelty, envy and slander, along with other wicked acts, and the twelve practices that belong to Brahmins, such as truth, self-control and learning.
shots.B05C043S03H01: Sanatsujata describes the six kinds of renunciation, from not rejoicing in prosperity and giving up rites, to giving up desire, not grieving at failure, not clinging to loved ones, and giving to the deserving.
shots.B05C043S03H02: Sanatsujata says the faults of pride are to be avoided, that self-knowledge has eight virtues, and that truth is the foundation of self-control, renunciation and self-knowledge.
shots.B05C043S03H03: Dhritarashtra asks which view of the Supreme is correct, since some teach one god, some three or four, and some only Brahman.
shots.B05C043S03H04: Sanatsujata says there is only one Brahman, which is truth, and that people split it into many gods out of ignorance. The person who seeks Brahman through truth finds what he needs at home, and those who have knowledge of the Self hold truth as the highest aim.
shots.B05C043S03H05: Sanatsujata says that knowledge bears fruit at once and asceticism later, that reading the Vedas alone does not make a Brahmin, and that the Self cannot be found by looking in any direction. Only one who knows the Self, is established in truth and can settle others' doubts is truly learned, and a Kshatriya who lives by these virtues can also see Brahman.

B05C044.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanatsujata to keep teaching about Brahman, which he calls rare because it is free of worldly desire. The sage says Brahman is reached only after the senses are restrained and the will is absorbed into pure intellect, through the discipline of brahmacharya under a teacher. He then describes the steps of a disciple's devotion and says that knowledge alone leads to liberation. Asked what Brahman looks like, he says it cannot be seen in any visible thing, and is the source and basis of all that exists.

scenes.B05C044S01: Dhritarashtra asks for more on Brahman, and Sanatsujata says it is reached through restraint and disciplined study.
scenes.B05C044S02: Sanatsujata describes the disciple's service to a teacher and the steps of brahmacharya, and then says that Brahman has no visible form.

shots.B05C044S01H01: Dhritarashtra praises the discourse on Brahman and the origin of the universe and asks Sanatsujata to go on with teaching free of worldly desire.
shots.B05C044S01H02: Sanatsujata says that Brahman cannot be reached quickly, and that after the senses are restrained and the will is absorbed into pure intellect, a state free of worldly thought follows, which is attained only through brahmacharya.
shots.B05C044S01H03: Dhritarashtra asks how immortality follows from Brahman, if its knowledge already dwells in the mind and needs no effort to show itself.
shots.B05C044S01H04: Sanatsujata explains that the knowledge is hidden in the mind and is revealed by pure intellect and brahmacharya, and that eminent teachers hold it. He offers to teach it.
shots.B05C044S01H05: Dhritarashtra asks what brahmacharya should be like so that knowledge of Brahman can be reached without great difficulty.
shots.B05C044S02H01: Sanatsujata describes the disciple who lives with his teacher and serves him in body, word and deed, honoring the teacher's family and giving back what he earns. He lists stages of this discipline and says the disciple who goes this way is rewarded with wealth, fame and liberation, while knowledge alone leads to Brahman.
shots.B05C044S02H02: Dhritarashtra asks what colour and shape Brahman has.
shots.B05C044S02H03: Sanatsujata says that Brahman cannot be seen in earth, sky, water, stars, Vedic texts or sacrifices, and that it is the basis of all things, one without duality, and the root from which creatures spring and to which they return.

B05C045.summary: Sanatsujata lists the faults that ruin human life, including greed, anger, pride, and jealousy, and the twelve virtues of a Brahmin, such as truth, restraint, and forgiveness. He describes the eighteen faults of arrogance and the signs of true friendship, including sharing a friend's sorrow and giving even what is dear when a friend truly needs it. He teaches that sacrifice performed without knowledge brings no lasting reward, and that the way to Brahman is restraint of the senses and the search within. The chapter ends with his statement that this teaching is the only true philosophy.

scenes.B05C045S01: Sanatsujata lists faults and virtues, the signs of true friendship, and the teaching that knowledge of Brahman, not sacrifice alone, leads to liberation.

shots.B05C045S01H01: Sanatsujata lists the twelve grave faults, the six kinds of wicked men, the seven kinds of sinful men, the twelve virtues of a Brahmin, and the eighteen faults of arrogance, and gives six signs of true friendship, including sharing a friend's joy and sorrow and giving even the dearest things when needed. He says that restraint of the senses is asceticism, that sacrifice without knowledge cannot reach immortality, and that the self should be sought in quiet restraint, with the mind kept free of pride and praise. He calls this the only true philosophy.

B05C046.summary: Sanatsujata gives a long hymn-like teaching on the primal Seed, the Supreme Brahman, which is beyond sight and is seen only by yogins with the inner eye. He describes the body as a chariot, the four states of the Self, and the unity of the Self in all beings, with the refrain that the Eternal One is seen by yogins with their mental eye. He says that the one who knows Brahman is not defiled by good or bad deeds, and ends with the words that the Universal Father dwells in the heart of every creature. The chapter presents the highest teaching of the Sanatsujata section.

scenes.B05C046S01: Sanatsujata teaches in a long hymn about the primal Seed, the Self in all beings, and the knower who is untouched by deeds.

shots.B05C046S01H01: Sanatsujata describes the primal Seed as pure knowledge that shines in the sun and the luminous bodies, that is seen by yogins with the mental eye, and that gives rise to the elements, the gods, the rivers and the living beings. He describes the body as a chariot, the four states of the Self, and the illusory stream of the world, and he says that the Self, though one, dwells in all, that the enlightened are free of good and bad deeds, and that the Universal Father is in every heart.

B05C047.summary: Dhritarashtra and his court spend the night listening to Sanatsujata and Vidura. In the morning the kings, the princes and the Kaurava leaders gather in a splendid hall to hear the envoy's report. Sanjaya returns from the Pandavas and announces his arrival, and he begins to tell the assembly what the Pandavas have sent. The chapter sets the stage for the formal reading of Yudhishthira's message.

scenes.B05C047S01: The night passes, the kings assemble in the hall, and Sanjaya returns from the Pandavas and prepares to deliver their message.

shots.B05C047S01H01: Vaisampayana reports that the king spends the night listening to Sanatsujata and Vidura, and that in the morning the kings and Kaurava leaders gather in the splendid hall. Sanjaya arrives in his chariot, greets the assembly, passes on the Pandavas' greetings, and says he will now report the message he was sent to deliver.

B05C048.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to repeat exactly what Arjuna said in reply to the Kaurava court. Sanjaya relays Arjuna's defiant message: if Duryodhana will not return the kingdom to Yudhishthira, the Kauravas will be destroyed in war. Arjuna names each Pandava hero, predicts that Duryodhana will repent in every battle, and says that Krishna is his ally by divine favor and by Krishna's own past deeds. The message closes with a warning that the Kauravas will perish if they fight, while also stating that the Pandavas wish the Kauravas to keep living.

scenes.B05C048S01: Sanjaya relays Arjuna's defiant reply to Duryodhana, naming the Pandava heroes, predicting Duryodhana's repentance, and warning of the destruction of the Kauravas if they fight.

shots.B05C048S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya, in front of his son and the kings, what Arjuna said.
shots.B05C048S01H02: Sanjaya relays Arjuna's long reply in the presence of Krishna: he demands the kingdom for Yudhishthira, names each Pandava hero and predicts Duryodhana's repentance in battle, recounts Krishna's past victories, claims divine favor and his own foresight, and warns that if the Kauravas fight they will all perish, though the Pandavas would be content if the Kauravas chose peace.

B05C049.summary: Bhishma warns Duryodhana with an old story: Nara and Narayana, two ancient sages who aided Indra, are the same beings as Arjuna and Krishna, so the Kauravas will face unbeatable foes. Karna answers with boasts that he will kill the Pandavas and that he is loyal to Duryodhana. Bhishma mocks Karna's record, recalling that Karna did nothing when Arjuna defeated the Kauravas and the Gandharvas, and Drona urges peace before war breaks out. Dhritarashtra does not answer them, and the Kauravas begin to lose hope.

scenes.B05C049S01: Bhishma tells the story of Nara and Narayana to warn Duryodhana, Karna boasts in reply, and Drona urges peace while the Kauravas lose hope.

shots.B05C049S01H01: Bhishma tells Duryodhana how the gods gathered before Brahma, and how two ancient sages, Nara and Narayana, left the assembly without honoring him. Brahma explains that they are mighty beings who exist to destroy the Asuras.
shots.B05C049S01H02: Bhishma recounts how Nara and Narayana helped Indra in battle, how Arjuna has defeated many foes, and how Krishna and Arjuna are the same two beings born again to fight. He warns that Duryodhana will remember this when he sees them together, and says that only Karna, Shakuni and Dussasana support him.
shots.B05C049S01H03: Karna replies that Bhishma should not speak to him this way, since he has kept his duties as a Kshatriya and will slay the Pandavas.
shots.B05C049S01H04: Bhishma says that Karna is not a sixteenth the equal of the Pandavas, and recalls that Karna was absent when Arjuna stripped the Kauravas of their robes at Virata and when the Gandharvas took Duryodhana captive, and that it was the Pandavas who rescued him.
shots.B05C049S01H05: Drona urges the king to accept peace before the war begins. Dhritarashtra pays no heed and again asks Sanjaya about the Pandavas, and the Kauravas give up hope.

B05C050.summary: Dhritarashtra asks how Yudhishthira is bearing the coming war and what forces the Pandavas have gathered. Sanjaya describes the Pandavas and their allies rejoicing and gathering around Yudhishthira, and when asked for the details of the forces he falls senseless. Once he recovers, he names the Pandava warriors and their allies one by one, from Dhrishtadyumna and Bhima to Krishna, Drupada and many kings.

scenes.B05C050S01: Dhritarashtra asks about Yudhishthira and the Pandava forces, and Sanjaya describes their joyful gathering before he falls senseless.
scenes.B05C050S02: Sanjaya recovers and names the Pandava warriors and allies one by one.

shots.B05C050S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks how Yudhishthira bears the coming strife, goaded by the deceptions of the Kaurava sons, and whether his brothers and sons await his orders.
shots.B05C050S01H02: Sanjaya says the Pandavas and their allies look to Yudhishthira and gather in joy, with cars, herdsmen, and many women coming to see Arjuna in armor.
shots.B05C050S01H03: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to list the forces of Dhrishtadyumna, the Somakas and the others arrayed against the Kauravas.
shots.B05C050S01H04: Sanjaya pauses, sighs deeply, and suddenly faints. Vidura tells the assembly that Sanjaya has fallen senseless.
shots.B05C050S01H05: Dhritarashtra suggests that Sanjaya is overcome by the sight of the mighty Pandavas.
shots.B05C050S02H01: Sanjaya recovers and names the Pandava warriors one by one: Dhrishtadyumna, Bhima, Arjuna, the twins, Shikhandin, Abhimanyu, Yuyudhana, Virata, the sons of Draupadi, Krishna, Drupada and many kings, each set against a specific Kaurava leader.

B05C051.summary: Dhritarashtra is terrified of Bhima, whose strength and mace he describes at length, and he recalls how Bhima overpowered his sons even as children. He mourns that his sons will be destroyed in battle and blames Duryodhana's dice match and the force of Time for the ruin of the Kurus. He ends in despair, saying he cannot see how to save his sons and that Bhima and Arjuna will destroy them.

scenes.B05C051S01: Dhritarashtra describes his terror of Bhima and his despair at the coming ruin of his sons.

shots.B05C051S01H01: Dhritarashtra admits he is terrified of Bhima, describes his strength and mace, recalls his childhood rivalry with Duryodhana and the other sons, and mourns the destruction he foresees. He blames the dice match and fate and asks Sanjaya where he can turn, concluding that his sons will be slain and that Bhima and Arjuna will destroy them.

B05C052.summary: Dhritarashtra despairs of victory, saying that Arjuna with Krishna as charioteer and the Gandiva bow is unbeatable, and that Drona and Karna would not stand against him for long. He recalls Arjuna's past triumphs, including his victory over the gods at Khandava, and says that his sons' follies have brought an unstoppable force against them. He sees omens of ruin all around and believes that the Bharatas will be destroyed.

scenes.B05C052S01: Dhritarashtra despairs of victory against Arjuna, recalls his past triumphs, and sees omens of the destruction of the Kurus.

shots.B05C052S01H01: Dhritarashtra says that no warrior can stand against Arjuna with Krishna as his charioteer, that Drona and Karna would not prevail, and that Arjuna's arrows will consume his troops. He recalls Arjuna's victory at Khandava and sees the omens of destruction, which he takes to mean that the Kurus will fall.

B05C053.summary: Dhritarashtra reflects that the Pandava side, with Krishna, Satyaki, Dhrishtadyumna and Yudhishthira's own virtue, is too strong for the Kauravas, and that he himself has treated the Pandavas unjustly. He urges his sons and the Kaurava leaders to consider peace, because the whole Kuru line would be destroyed in a war. The king's fears have turned into a plea for a settlement.

scenes.B05C053S01: Dhritarashtra admits the Pandavas are too strong and urges the Kauravas to consider peace to avoid the ruin of the Kurus.

shots.B05C053S01H01: Dhritarashtra describes the Pandava allies as eager to die for their cause, names Krishna, Satyaki and Dhrishtadyumna as formidable, and admits that he fears the wrath of Yudhishthira, Arjuna and the twins. He says he has acted deceitfully toward Yudhishthira, and urges the Kauravas to consider peace, since Yudhishthira would not be indifferent to their distress.

B05C054.summary: Sanjaya answers Dhritarashtra with a sharp rebuke. He says the king has always taken his sons' side, laughed when the Pandavas lost at dice, and never restrained the cruelty shown to them. He reminds the king that Arjuna once rescued the Kauravas from the Gandharvas, and that Arjuna, his bow, and his charioteer are unmatched. He concludes that the king's grief now comes too late, and that Duryodhana's hostility should be checked.

scenes.B05C054S01: Sanjaya rebukes Dhritarashtra for backing his sons, reminds him of Arjuna's feats and the Pandavas' allies, and tells him that his grief is too late.

shots.B05C054S01H01: Sanjaya agrees that the Kshatriyas will be destroyed by Arjuna's bow, asks why the king follows his sons' counsel, and says that a father who harms his children is not a father. He recalls how the king laughed at the Pandavas' defeat, how Arjuna rescued the Kauravas from the Gandharvas, how Krishna and Arjuna are unmatched, and how the kings have turned to the Pandavas. He says the king should check Duryodhana and stop his lament.

B05C055.summary: Duryodhana answers his father's fears with boasts. He recalls that when the Pandavas were in exile, Krishna and the allied kings urged Yudhishthira to reclaim his kingdom, and that the Kaurava elders vowed to defend the Kuru throne. He claims that his skill with the mace makes him a match for Bhima, lists the Kaurava champions, and says that his eleven akshauhinis far outnumber the Pandava forces. He tells Sanjaya to continue with news of the Pandavas.

scenes.B05C055S01: Duryodhana recalls the Kaurava elders' pledge, boasts of his mace and of the Kaurava champions, and claims superior numbers before asking Sanjaya for more news.

shots.B05C055S01H01: Duryodhana says there is no need to fear, recalls how Krishna and the allied kings urged Yudhishthira to reclaim the kingdom during the exile, and how he asked Bhishma, Drona and Kripa for counsel and was told to stand firm. He notes that the elders promised to defeat any enemy and vowed that Bhishma's strength was unmatched.
shots.B05C055S01H02: Duryodhana boasts that he is unmatched with the mace and expects to kill Bhima with a single blow, lists the Kaurava warriors and the strength of Karna and Bhishma, and says that his eleven akshauhinis are more than the seven the Pandavas command. He says Yudhishthira seeks only five villages and that the Kauravas need not fear.
shots.B05C055S01H03: Duryodhana asks Sanjaya again about the doings of the Pandavas.

B05C056.summary: Duryodhana asks Sanjaya how the Pandavas are preparing, and Sanjaya reports that Yudhishthira and his brothers are cheerful and confident. Arjuna, seeing omens, declares that victory will be theirs. Duryodhana asks about Arjuna's car and banner, and Sanjaya describes the celestial chariot, its magical banner, and the heavenly steeds given to each of the Pandavas.

scenes.B05C056S01: Duryodhana asks about the Pandava preparations, and Sanjaya reports their confidence and describes Arjuna's magical chariot and horses.

shots.B05C056S01H01: Duryodhana asks what Yudhishthira and his allies are doing now that they have an army of seven akshauhinis.
shots.B05C056S01H02: Sanjaya reports that Yudhishthira and his brothers are cheerful, that the twins are fearless, and that Arjuna, testing his new mantras, declared that victory is certain.
shots.B05C056S01H03: Duryodhana, sneering at the Pandavas' defeat at dice, asks what horses are yoked to Arjuna's car and what banners fly on it.
shots.B05C056S01H04: Sanjaya describes the celestial car made by divine artisans, its banner that covers a yojana and bears Hanuman's image, and the heavenly horses given by Chitrasena and Indra to each of the Pandava brothers and the sons of Subhadra and Draupadi.

B05C057.summary: Sanjaya lists the Pandava allies who have arrived, including Krishna, Satyaki, Drupada and his sons, Virata, the kings of Magadha and Chedi, and the Kekaya princes, and reports how each Kaurava champion has been assigned to a Pandava warrior. Dhritarashtra despairs that his foolish sons will be crushed by the Pandavas, while Duryodhana insists that the Kauravas are strong enough to win. Sanjaya then reports Dhrishtadyumna's fierce vow to fight and Dhrishtadyumna's message urging the Kauravas to surrender the kingdom before Arjuna destroys them.

scenes.B05C057S01: Sanjaya lists the Pandava allies and their assigned opponents, Dhritarashtra despairs, and Duryodhana insists on war.
scenes.B05C057S02: Sanjaya reports Dhrishtadyumna's vow to fight and his message that the Kauravas should surrender the kingdom.

shots.B05C057S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks who has come to the Pandavas' side and who will fight his son's forces.
shots.B05C057S01H02: Sanjaya lists the allies: Krishna, Satyaki, Chekitana, Drupada with his sons, Virata with his sons, the kings of Magadha and Chedi, and the Kekaya princes. He then lists the assignments, such as Bhishma to Shikhandin, Duryodhana to Bhima, Karna and Jayadratha to Arjuna, and the Kaurava princes to Subhadra's son, and the Pandava army is arranged.
shots.B05C057S01H03: Dhritarashtra despairs, saying the Pandavas with Krishna, Arjuna, Bhima, Dhrishtadyumna, Satyaki, Drupada and many others are invincible, and that his foolish sons insist on fighting them.
shots.B05C057S01H04: Duryodhana tells his father that both sides share the same earth, that the Kaurava champions are invincible, and that the Pandavas cannot even look at his troops, so the kings will capture the Pandavas.
shots.B05C057S01H05: Dhritarashtra calls his son mad, says that Yudhishthira cannot be beaten, that Bhishma does not want to fight the Pandavas, and asks Sanjaya for news of their movements.
shots.B05C057S02H01: Sanjaya reports Dhrishtadyumna's vow to fight the Kaurava host alone, and Yudhishthira's request that he lead. Dhrishtadyumna sends Sanjaya to tell the Kauravas to yield the kingdom before Arjuna, protected by the gods, destroys them.

B05C058.summary: Dhritarashtra pleads with Duryodhana to make peace, arguing that war is never good, that half the earth is enough for him, and that Karna, Dussasana and Shakuni are leading him astray. Duryodhana refuses and declares that he and Karna alone will fight the Pandavas, describing the battle as a sacrifice and vowing not to yield even a needle's point of land. Dhritarashtra then disowns his son, foresees the Kuru army being crushed by Bhima and Satyaki, and asks Sanjaya for more news.

scenes.B05C058S01: Dhritarashtra pleads for peace, Duryodhana refuses, and Dhritarashtra disowns him and foresees the Kuru army's ruin.
