shots.B05C058S01H01: Dhritarashtra says Yudhishthira has the strength of a Kshatriya and has lived the life of a brahmachari, urges Duryodhana to give back the Pandavas' share, and says that the Kauravas deem peace just. He blames Karna, Dussasana and Shakuni for pushing his son toward war, and says that none of the elders wants war.
shots.B05C058S01H02: Duryodhana refuses to rely on his elders and declares that he and Karna and Dussasana will fight the Pandavas. He compares the war to a sacrifice with its own altar, weapons and offerings, with Yudhishthira as the victim, and vows that he will not yield even a needle's point of land.
shots.B05C058S01H03: Dhritarashtra disowns Duryodhana, grieves for the kings who follow him, and foresees Bhima and Satyaki breaking the Kaurava ranks, with the elephants and chariots scattered and the army crushed, and urges his son to remember his warning.
shots.B05C058S01H04: Vaisampayana reports that after speaking to the kings, Dhritarashtra turns and asks Sanjaya another question.

B05C059.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to report everything Krishna and Arjuna said. Sanjaya describes finding the two at ease in the inner chambers and relays Krishna's message to the Kuru elders, warning of danger and stating that no one can match Arjuna in battle. Arjuna backs him up. The chapter shows the Kuru king hearing from his envoy how formidable the Pandava side is.

scenes.B05C059S01: Sanjaya reports to Dhritarashtra on his visit to Krishna and Arjuna and the message they sent to the Kurus.

shots.B05C059S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to tell him in full what Krishna and Arjuna said.
shots.B05C059S01H02: Sanjaya describes the two heroes in the inner chambers, relays Krishna's warning to the Kuru elders, and quotes Krishna saying no one can match Arjuna, citing the Virata episode; Arjuna then agrees.

B05C060.summary: Vaisampayana reports that Dhritarashtra weighs the strength of both sides after hearing Sanjaya and concludes the Pandavas are stronger. He admits his fear to Duryodhana, expecting the gods and Agni to aid the Pandavas, and names Arjuna's bow and chariot as especially dangerous. He says he prefers peace to war. The chapter records the king's private doubts before the war begins.

scenes.B05C060S01: Dhritarashtra weighs the two armies, judges the Pandavas stronger, and voices his fear to Duryodhana.

shots.B05C060S01H01: Dhritarashtra weighs the two sides, judges the Pandavas stronger, and tells Duryodhana he fears divine help for Arjuna and prefers peace.

B05C061.summary: Duryodhana answers his father's fear with anger, arguing that the gods act without desire and so will not help the Pandavas. He boasts of his own power over nature, snakes and armies, and predicts the Pandavas will be destroyed by him. He then asks Sanjaya again about Yudhishthira's war plans. The chapter shows the prince's overconfidence set against his father's caution.

scenes.B05C061S01: Duryodhana, angry at his father, boasts of his own power and predicts the Pandavas' defeat, then asks about Yudhishthira's war plans.

shots.B05C061S01H01: Duryodhana argues the gods, free of desire, will not help the Pandavas, then boasts of his power over nature and foes and predicts their defeat at his hands.
shots.B05C061S01H02: Duryodhana asks Sanjaya again to learn what Yudhishthira is planning for war.

B05C062.summary: Karna, unasked, says Rama cursed him for winning the Brahma weapon by deceit, but he still has it and vows to defeat the Pandavas alone. Bhishma rebukes him, warning that Krishna protects Arjuna. Karna admits Krishna's greatness, lays down his weapons, and says he will fight only in the court. Bhishma then mocks him, and the chapter turns to Duryodhana.

scenes.B05C062S01: Karna boasts of his Brahma weapon and vows to defeat the Pandavas, Bhishma rebukes him, and Karna lays down his weapons.

shots.B05C062S01H01: Karna vows to slay the Pandavas despite Rama's curse, and Bhishma warns him that Krishna protects Arjuna and that Karna's weapons would fail against him.
shots.B05C062S01H02: Karna admits Krishna's greatness, lays down his weapons, and says he will appear only in the court and not on the battlefield.
shots.B05C062S01H03: Karna leaves, Bhishma laughs at his broken promises and says he lost his virtue by deceiving Rama, and Duryodhana then turns to Bhishma.

B05C063.summary: Duryodhana claims the Pandavas are ordinary men no stronger than the Kurus, and vows that he, Karna and Dussasana will kill them. Vidura replies with a long teaching on self-restraint, listing its virtues and the marks of a self-restrained person. The chapter sets the prince's boasting against the counsel of restraint.

scenes.B05C063S01: Duryodhana boasts he will defeat the Pandavas, and Vidura answers with a long teaching on self-restraint.

shots.B05C063S01H01: Duryodhana says the Pandavas are only men and that he, Karna and Dussasana will kill them, and Vidura replies with a long teaching on self-restraint and its marks.

B05C064.summary: Vidura tells Dhritarashtra a parable: a fowler's net catches two birds, which quarrel and fall into his hands, showing that kinsmen who fight over wealth become easy prey. He then recounts hunters who died trying to reach a jar of honey guarded by snakes, and warns that Duryodhana is blind to his own ruin in the same way. He urges the king to make peace with Yudhishthira.

scenes.B05C064S01: Vidura tells a parable about quarrelling birds and a story of hunters who died seeking honey, then urges peace with the Pandavas.

shots.B05C064S01H01: A hermit asks a fowler why he chases two birds that flew off with his net, and the fowler answers that they will quarrel and fall to him.
shots.B05C064S01H02: The birds quarrel and are caught, which Vidura applies to kinsmen who fight over wealth; he then tells of hunters who died seeking a honey jar guarded by snakes, likens Duryodhana to them, and urges the king to make peace with Yudhishthira.

B05C065.summary: Dhritarashtra pleads with his son Duryodhana to give up his course. He names the Pandava champions, Yudhishthira, Bhimasena, Arjuna, Dhrishtadyumna, Satyaki and Krishna, and says none can be easily beaten. He urges Duryodhana to accept the counsel of Bhishma, Drona and the other elders, and to share the kingdom with his cousins.

scenes.B05C065S01: Dhritarashtra pleads with Duryodhana to heed the elders and make peace, listing the Pandava champions he would face.

shots.B05C065S01H01: Dhritarashtra warns Duryodhana that he has misjudged the Pandavas, lists their champions, and urges him to follow the elders and share the kingdom with his cousins.

B05C066.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to repeat Arjuna's reply after Krishna's speech. Sanjaya relays Arjuna's warning that the Kaurava kings are doomed unless they return Yudhishthira's share, and otherwise Arjuna will send them to death. Sanjaya then says he has delivered the message and taken leave of Arjuna and Krishna.

scenes.B05C066S01: Sanjaya passes on Arjuna's reply to the Kaurava kings and says he has delivered the message.

shots.B05C066S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to report what Arjuna said after Krishna's speech, since he is eager to hear it.
shots.B05C066S01H02: Sanjaya relays Arjuna's message that the assembled kings are doomed and must return Yudhishthira's share or face his arrows, then says he has come back with that message.

B05C067.summary: After Duryodhana ignores Sanjaya's message and the kings withdraw, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya privately which side will fall. Sanjaya asks that Vyasa and Gandhari be present so he can speak without the king's ill will. Vyasa, now in the court, tells Sanjaya to tell the king all he knows about Vasudeva and Arjuna.

scenes.B05C067S01: After the kings leave, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya privately about the two armies, and Vyasa and Gandhari are called to hear the answer.

shots.B05C067S01H01: Duryodhana pays little heed to Sanjaya and the kings leave, so Dhritarashtra privately asks Sanjaya which side will be destroyed and how strong each is.
shots.B05C067S01H02: Sanjaya refuses to answer in secret for fear of the king's anger, and asks that Vyasa and Gandhari be brought in to hear him.
shots.B05C067S01H03: Vyasa and Gandhari enter the court, and Vyasa tells Sanjaya to tell the king everything he knows about Vasudeva and Arjuna.

B05C068.summary: Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that Arjuna and Krishna are godlike equals, and he describes Krishna's discus and his past victories over demons and kings. He argues that Krishna is the supreme Lord who will use the Pandavas to destroy Duryodhana's sinful sons. Those who know him are not deceived by his illusion.

scenes.B05C068S01: Sanjaya presents Krishna as the supreme Lord, whose power outweighs the universe and who will bring about the Kauravas' downfall.

shots.B05C068S01H01: Sanjaya describes Arjuna and Krishna as godlike equals, praises Krishna's discus and his past victories, and says Krishna, the Lord of time, will use the Pandavas to destroy Duryodhana's wicked sons.

B05C069.summary: Dhritarashtra asks how Sanjaya can know Krishna as the Supreme Lord when he himself cannot. Sanjaya explains that faith and wisdom give him that knowledge, and that the king must subdue his senses to reach it. Duryodhana refuses to submit to Krishna even if he were to destroy mankind, and Gandhari and Vyasa rebuke the king and urge him to listen.

scenes.B05C069S01: Dhritarashtra asks how Sanjaya knows Krishna, Sanjaya explains his faith, and Dhritarashtra urges Duryodhana to seek Krishna's protection.
scenes.B05C069S02: Duryodhana refuses to submit to Krishna, Dhritarashtra and Gandhari rebuke him, and Vyasa urges the king to heed Sanjaya.
scenes.B05C069S03: Sanjaya says a person with an uncontrolled mind cannot know Krishna and urges the king to subdue his senses through wisdom.

shots.B05C069S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks how Sanjaya has come to know Madhava as the Supreme Lord when he himself cannot.
shots.B05C069S01H02: Sanjaya answers that the king lacks knowledge while his own is intact, and says he knows Krishna as the source and end of all things.
shots.B05C069S01H03: Dhritarashtra asks what faith lets Sanjaya know Janardana in this way.
shots.B05C069S01H04: Sanjaya says he has no regard for worldly illusion or empty rites, and that his faith has purified him so that he knows Janardana from the scriptures.
shots.B05C069S01H05: Dhritarashtra tells Duryodhana to seek Krishna's protection, calling Sanjaya a trusted friend who can guide him.
shots.B05C069S02H01: Duryodhana says he will not submit to Krishna even if Krishna, allied with Arjuna, destroyed all mankind.
shots.B05C069S02H02: Dhritarashtra calls his son envious, wicked and vain, and says he is set on his own ruin.
shots.B05C069S02H03: Gandhari rebukes Duryodhana for his greed and defiance, and warns that he will be struck down by Bhimasena.
shots.B05C069S02H04: Vyasa tells the king that Sanjaya can lead him to safety, and that people lacking contentment fall into death like blind men led by the blind.
shots.B05C069S02H05: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to name the path that would let him attain Hrishikesa and find salvation.
shots.B05C069S03H01: Sanjaya says Krishna cannot be known by one with an uncontrolled mind, that sacrifice without self-control is useless, and that subduing the senses through true wisdom is the path.

B05C070.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to explain the names of Krishna, hoping that knowing their meaning will help him reach the Supreme Being. Sanjaya lists many of Krishna's names and gives their meanings, such as Vasudeva, Hrishikesa and Janardana. He ends by saying the slayer of Madhu will come to prevent the slaughter of the Kurus.

scenes.B05C070S01: Sanjaya explains many names of Krishna and their meanings, then predicts that Krishna will come to stop the Kurus' destruction.

shots.B05C070S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to tell him again about Krishna's names, hoping their meaning will help him know the Supreme Being.
shots.B05C070S01H02: Sanjaya lists many of Krishna's names with the meanings given to them, and closes by saying the slayer of Madhu will come to prevent the Kurus' slaughter.

B05C071.summary: Dhritarashtra says he envies those who will see Krishna in person. He praises Krishna at length as eternal, supreme and the creator of the three worlds. He places himself in Krishna's hands and calls on him by many names. The chapter reflects the king's reverence and longing even as he remains committed to the war.

scenes.B05C071S01: Dhritarashtra praises Krishna at length, envies those who can see him, and places himself in his hands.

shots.B05C071S01H01: Dhritarashtra envies those who will see Krishna in person, praises him in many epithets, and places himself in his hands.

B05C072.summary: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did after Sanjaya returned to the Kurus. Yudhishthira turns to Krishna for help, listing the Kauravas' broken faith and the miseries of poverty, and says he would rather have peace than war. Krishna agrees to go to the Kuru court to try to make peace, and Yudhishthira reluctantly consents.

scenes.B05C072S01: Yudhishthira asks Krishna for help, laying out the Pandavas' grievances and the miseries of poverty and dishonour.
scenes.B05C072S02: Yudhishthira argues against war and asks Krishna's counsel, and Krishna agrees to go to the Kuru court despite Yudhishthira's fears.

shots.B05C072S01H01: Heading: names the Bhagwat Yana Parva section.
shots.B05C072S01H02: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did after Sanjaya went back to the Kurus.
shots.B05C072S01H03: Yudhishthira turns to Krishna, asking him to protect the Pandavas now that Duryodhana has refused their share of the kingdom.
shots.B05C072S01H04: Krishna replies that he is ready to do whatever Yudhishthira asks.
shots.B05C072S01H05: Yudhishthira says Dhritarashtra and Duryodhana have broken faith, recalls the Pandavas' loyal exile, and then dwells at length on the miseries of poverty, the value of wealth, and the role of shame and wisdom in virtue.
shots.B05C072S02H01: Yudhishthira argues that war is sinful and costly to both sides, prefers humiliation to bloodshed, and asks Krishna what would preserve their interests and their virtue.
shots.B05C072S02H02: Vaisampayana says Krishna agrees to go to the Kuru court, hoping to make peace without harming the Pandavas' interests.
shots.B05C072S02H03: Yudhishthira objects that Duryodhana will not heed Krishna and that Krishna should not walk into a hall full of hostile kings.
shots.B05C072S02H04: Krishna replies that going will spare them blame whatever the outcome, and that no kings can stand against him in battle when he is enraged.
shots.B05C072S02H05: Yudhishthira consents, hopes Krishna returns successful, and asks him to speak whatever will benefit the Pandavas.

B05C073.summary: Krishna tells Yudhishthira that a Kshatriya should not live by begging and that Duryodhana cannot be trusted to keep peace. He recalls the Kauravas' crimes, including the crooked dice game and the humiliation of Draupadi, and calls Duryodhana deserving of death. He agrees to make one attempt at peace, but he expects war, citing omens, and tells the Pandavas to prepare.

scenes.B05C073S01: Krishna says Kshatriyas must fight rather than beg, lists the Kauravas' crimes, and says he will try for peace but expects war.

shots.B05C073S01H01: Krishna tells Yudhishthira that a Kshatriya should not beg, recalls the dice game and Draupadi's humiliation, calls Duryodhana deserving of death, promises to try for peace, and predicts war from the omens.

B05C074.summary: Bhima urges Krishna to address Duryodhana gently, describing him as proud, wicked and hard to teach. He warns that war will destroy the Bharatas, recalls earlier kings who destroyed their own kin, and would accept humiliation to avoid that ruin. He asks the elders to mediate, and the chapter closes with the start of the next section.

scenes.B05C074S01: Bhima urges Krishna to speak mildly to Duryodhana, warns of ruin for the family, and asks the elders to mediate.

shots.B05C074S01H01: Bhima urges Krishna to address Duryodhana gently, calls him wicked and hard to teach, warns that war will destroy the Bharatas, and asks the elders to mediate.

B05C075.summary: Krishna laughs at Bhima's sudden plea for peace and reminds him of his nightly rage and his oath to kill Duryodhana with his mace. He calls the change of heart a sign of fear, and urges Bhima to stand firm, since a Kshatriya should only enjoy what he wins by his own prowess. The exchange shows Krishna deliberately provoking Bhima's courage.

scenes.B05C075S01: Krishna laughs at Bhima's softened tone and reminds him of his wrath and his oath to kill Duryodhana.

shots.B05C075S01H01: Krishna laughs at Bhima's plea for peace, recalls his nightly rage and his oath to kill Duryodhana with his mace, and calls his change of heart a sign of fear.

B05C076.summary: Bhima, stung by Krishna's rebuke, replies that Krishna does not know his real strength and boasts that he could hold earth and sky apart. He says he could trample the Kshatriyas who oppose the Pandavas. He claims he restrains himself only out of compassion for the Bharata race.

scenes.B05C076S01: Bhima boasts of his strength, says he feels no fear, and claims he is holding back only for the sake of the Bharatas.

shots.B05C076S01H01: Bhima, stung by Krishna's rebuke, boasts of his unmatched strength, says he could crush the Kshatriyas, and claims he restrains himself only out of compassion for the Bharatas.

B05C077.summary: Krishna explains that his harsh words were meant to draw out Bhima's real mind, not to reproach him. He argues that human action has uncertain results, so one must act while accepting both fate and effort, without being broken by failure. He promises to seek peace at court, and says that if war comes he will drive Arjuna's chariot.

scenes.B05C077S01: Krishna explains that his harsh words were meant to test Bhima, promises to seek peace, and says he will drive Arjuna's chariot if war comes.

shots.B05C077S01H01: Krishna says his words were meant to test Bhima's resolve, explains that human action and fate combine unpredictably, promises to seek peace at court, and says he will drive Arjuna's chariot if war comes.

B05C078.summary: Arjuna agrees that Yudhishthira has spoken well, but asks Krishna to try for peace anyway, since Krishna is the friend of both sides. He recalls Duryodhana's crooked dice game and the insult to Draupadi, and says Duryodhana deserves death. He doubts that Duryodhana will ever deal justly with the Pandavas.

scenes.B05C078S01: Arjuna asks Krishna to try for peace while recalling Duryodhana's crimes and doubting that he will deal fairly.

shots.B05C078S01H01: Arjuna says peace may be possible if properly proposed and urges Krishna to try, then recalls Duryodhana's dice fraud and Draupadi's insult and doubts he will ever act justly.

B05C079.summary: Krishna says he will strive for peace, but notes that fate can defeat human effort, so success is not certain. He calls Duryodhana wicked and expects him to refuse to give back the kingdom, supported by Sakuni, Karna and Dussasana. He reminds Arjuna of the earlier cattle raid of Virata and rebukes him for doubting his commitment.

scenes.B05C079S01: Krishna says human effort and fate both matter, promises to do his best, and doubts Duryodhana will yield.

shots.B05C079S01H01: Krishna says he will try for peace though fate may defeat human effort, calls Duryodhana wicked and expects him to refuse, and rebukes Arjuna for doubting his commitment to the Pandavas.

B05C080.summary: Nakula says the Pandavas' circumstances have changed since their exile, and they now have a great army. He advises Krishna to speak mildly to Duryodhana first and then turn to threats, so that the prince grows afraid. He names the great warriors on the Pandava side and expects Krishna's persuasion, with the help of Vidura and the elders, to carry weight.

scenes.B05C080S01: Nakula says circumstances have changed and advises Krishna to speak mildly, then threaten, when he meets the Kurus.

shots.B05C080S01H01: Nakula says the situation has changed since the exile, the Pandavas now have a great army, and Krishna should begin with mild words and then turn to threats to make Duryodhana afraid.

B05C081.summary: Sahadeva insists that war must come, and urges Krishna to provoke it even if the Kauravas offer peace, since only Duryodhana's death can answer the insult to Draupadi. Satyaki agrees and reminds Krishna of the Pandavas' suffering in the forest. The assembled warriors roar their approval and show their eagerness to fight.

scenes.B05C081S01: Sahadeva and Satyaki call for war against Duryodhana, and the assembled warriors roar their approval.

shots.B05C081S01H01: Sahadeva says war must come and urges Krishna to provoke it, since his anger over Draupadi's insult can only be appeased by Duryodhana's death.
shots.B05C081S01H02: Satyaki agrees that Duryodhana must die, recalls the Pandavas in rags in the forest, and says the warriors assembled all back Sahadeva.
shots.B05C081S01H03: The warriors roar, cry out in praise of Satyaki, and show their eagerness to fight.

B05C082.summary: Draupadi, weeping, reminds Krishna of the dice game, the Pandavas' modest request for five villages, and her own humiliation in the assembly. She argues that peace with such enemies is hopeless and asks Krishna to direct his wrath at Dhritarashtra's sons. Krishna comforts her with a vow that the Kauravas will fall and her husbands will prosper.

scenes.B05C082S01: Draupadi, weeping, recounts her humiliation and urges Krishna to punish the Kauravas, and Krishna comforts her with a vow of victory.

shots.B05C082S01H01: Draupadi says Duryodhana cheated the Pandavas, notes that they asked only for five villages, argues that peace is hopeless, and recalls her humiliation in the assembly.
shots.B05C082S01H02: Draupadi grips her braid, recalls Dussasana's hands, and says she will rest only when he is dead; Krishna comforts her and vows the Kauravas will fall.

B05C083.summary: Arjuna urges Krishna to act as the friend of both sides and to warn Duryodhana of the consequences of refusing good counsel. Krishna agrees, and at dawn sets out in his chariot with Satyaki, amid omens, blessings from sages and the escort of the Pandavas and many kings. Yudhishthira asks Krishna to greet their mother and the elders, and Arjuna repeats his threat of war if the kingdom is not returned.

scenes.B05C083S01: Arjuna and Yudhishthira send Krishna off on his mission to Hastinapura, and Krishna sets out amid omens and blessings.

shots.B05C083S01H01: Arjuna urges Krishna to bring about peace and to tell Duryodhana that refusing good counsel will bring his own ruin.
shots.B05C083S01H02: Krishna agrees to go to Dhritarashtra, aiming for what is righteous and good for all.
shots.B05C083S01H03: At dawn Krishna sets out in his chariot amid auspicious signs, sages and birds blessing him, and the Pandavas and kings following, until Yudhishthira embraces him and begins his instructions.
shots.B05C083S01H04: Yudhishthira asks Krishna to greet and comfort their mother, the elders, Bhishma, Drona and Vidura, and then Arjuna repeats that the kingdom must be returned or the Kshatriyas will be destroyed.
shots.B05C083S01H05: Bhima roars in approval, Krishna drives on, and sages on the road ask him to speak wisely at the assembly they wish to attend.

B05C084.summary: Vaisampayana describes Krishna's escort of car-warriors, foot-soldiers and horsemen as he heads to Hastinapura. Janamejaya asks about the omens, and Vaisampayana describes frightening natural signs at the start of the journey, followed by a warm welcome along the road. Krishna spends the night at Vrikasthala, feasting Brahmanas who host him.

scenes.B05C084S01: Krishna sets out for Hastinapura with an escort, and omens mark his journey; he spends the night at Vrikasthala.

shots.B05C084S01H01: Ten car-warriors, a thousand foot-soldiers and a thousand horsemen, with attendants and provisions, follow Krishna on his journey to Hastinapura.
shots.B05C084S01H02: Janamejaya asks how Krishna travelled and what omens appeared as he left.
shots.B05C084S01H03: Vaisampayana lists the unsettling omens at Krishna's departure, then describes the welcome he receives along the road and his night's rest at Vrikasthala among honouring Brahmanas.

B05C085.summary: Dhritarashtra learns from spies that Krishna is coming and urges his elders and sons to give him a grand welcome. Duryodhana builds lavish pavilions and sends gifts, women and garlands along the road. Krishna ignores all of it and goes straight to the Kuru capital.

scenes.B05C085S01: Dhritarashtra orders a lavish welcome for Krishna, Duryodhana prepares pavilions, and Krishna passes them by.

shots.B05C085S01H01: Dhritarashtra, hearing from spies that Krishna is coming, asks the elders to prepare a grand welcome, and Duryodhana builds pavilions and sends gifts, but Krishna ignores them all.

B05C086.summary: Dhritarashtra tells Vidura that Krishna will arrive the next day, praising him as the leader of the Vrishnis. He lists the lavish honours he plans, including gold cars, elephants, servants, blankets, a precious gem and a procession of his sons, all but Duryodhana. He also orders Dussasana's mansion made ready as Krishna's lodging.

scenes.B05C086S01: Dhritarashtra tells Vidura he plans lavish gifts and a grand welcome for Krishna.

shots.B05C086S01H01: Dhritarashtra tells Vidura that Krishna will arrive tomorrow and lists the gifts, processions and cleaning of Dussasana's mansion he has ordered in his honour.

B05C087.summary: Vidura rebukes Dhritarashtra, saying the lavish gifts are a deception meant to win Krishna away from the Pandavas. He points out that the king refuses even five villages to his nephews, and says Krishna cannot be bought because of his bond with Arjuna. He urges the king to make peace and treat the Pandavas as his own sons.

scenes.B05C087S01: Vidura tells Dhritarashtra his lavish hospitality is a deception and urges him to make peace with the Pandavas.

shots.B05C087S01H01: Vidura tells Dhritarashtra that his lavish gifts are a deception meant to lure Krishna away from the Pandavas, which cannot work, and urges him to make peace and treat the Pandavas as sons.

B05C088.summary: Duryodhana dismisses Vidura's advice, saying Krishna should not be honoured because war is already decided. Bhishma reminds him that Krishna cannot be treated with disrespect and urges peace through Krishna. Duryodhana then proposes to imprison Krishna, Dhritarashtra rejects the plan, and Bhishma, furious, leaves the court.

scenes.B05C088S01: Duryodhana refuses to honour Krishna and proposes to imprison him, while Bhishma and Dhritarashtra object.
scenes.B05C088S02: Bhishma, furious at Duryodhana, rises and leaves the court.

shots.B05C088S01H01: Duryodhana says Krishna is devoted to the Pandavas and should not be honoured, since that would look like fear and war is already decided.
shots.B05C088S01H02: Bhishma tells Duryodhana that Krishna cannot be disrespected and urges him to seek peace through Krishna's good offices.
shots.B05C088S01H03: Duryodhana declares his plan to imprison Krishna when he arrives the next morning, so that the Pandavas and Vrishnis will submit, and asks how to do it unnoticed.
shots.B05C088S01H04: Dhritarashtra, pained, forbids the plan, noting that Krishna came as an envoy and has done no wrong.
shots.B05C088S01H05: Bhishma calls Duryodhana wicked, says his hour has come, and refuses to listen to such a sinful man any longer.
shots.B05C088S02H01: Bhishma rises in anger and leaves the place.

B05C089.summary: Krishna leaves Vrikasthala at dawn and is welcomed into Hastinapura by the Kauravas, except Duryodhana, and by crowds of citizens. He is honoured in Dhritarashtra's palace and then visits Vidura's house. There Vidura asks after the Pandavas, and Krishna begins to tell him all they have done.

scenes.B05C089S01: Krishna enters Hastinapura to a crowd's welcome, is honoured by Dhritarashtra, and then visits Vidura.

shots.B05C089S01H01: Krishna leaves Vrikasthala at dawn, is welcomed by the Kauravas except Duryodhana and the crowds, is honoured in Dhritarashtra's palace, then visits Vidura's house and begins to tell him of the Pandavas.

B05C090.summary: Krishna visits his aunt Pritha (Kunti), who weeps over her sons' hardships and asks after each of them. She blames her own father for giving her away and sends messages urging her sons to act with Kshatriya courage rather than live on others' charity. Krishna comforts her, and she accepts his words as true. He then leaves for Duryodhana's mansion.

scenes.B05C090S01: Krishna visits Pritha, who grieves for her sons and sends them messages urging courage, and Krishna comforts her.
scenes.B05C090S02: Krishna takes his leave of Pritha and sets out for Duryodhana's mansion.

shots.B05C090S01H01: Krishna visits his aunt Pritha, who embraces him and asks after each of her sons and Draupadi, speaking with tears of their suffering in exile.
shots.B05C090S01H02: Pritha laments the dice game, the exile and the insult to Draupadi, blames her own father for giving her away, and recalls a prophecy that Arjuna would conquer the world.
shots.B05C090S01H03: Pritha sends messages to Yudhishthira, Bhima and Arjuna urging them to act as Kshatriyas and not to live on others' charity, and to avenge Draupadi's insult.
shots.B05C090S01H04: Krishna comforts her, calling her a lady of great virtue and telling her that her sons, though suffering now, will soon prosper and prevail.
shots.B05C090S01H05: Pritha, comforted, tells Krishna to act without guile, praises his truth and lineage, and says his words must be true.
shots.B05C090S02H01: Krishna takes leave of Pritha, walks round her, and departs for Duryodhana's mansion.

B05C091.summary: Krishna goes to Duryodhana's palace, where he is honoured but declines the feast Duryodhana offers, saying envoys eat only once their mission succeeds. He rebukes Duryodhana for his unreasoning hatred of the Pandavas and says he will eat only Vidura's food. He leaves for Vidura's house, where the Kauravas offer him their homes, and he dines there on food Kunti prepares, after feeding Brahmanas first.

scenes.B05C091S01: Krishna visits Duryodhana, refuses his feast, rebukes his hatred of the Pandavas, and dines at Vidura's house.

shots.B05C091S01H01: Krishna enters Duryodhana's palace, is honoured by the court, and declines the feast Duryodhana offers, asking Krishna why he refuses.
shots.B05C091S01H02: Krishna replies that envoys eat only after their mission succeeds, and Duryodhana complains that his courtesy deserves better and insists he has no quarrel with Krishna.
shots.B05C091S01H03: Krishna says he would never abandon virtue, condemns Duryodhana's hatred of the Pandavas as unreasonable and sinful, and declares he will eat only Vidura's food.
shots.B05C091S01H04: Krishna leaves the palace for Vidura's house, where Drona, Kripa, Bhishma and other Kauravas offer him their homes and wealth.
shots.B05C091S01H05: Krishna thanks them but declines, and after Vidura hosts him, Kunti serves him food, which he shares first with Brahmanas and then with his attendants.

B05C092.summary: After Krishna has dined, Vidura warns him during the night that his mission is ill-judged. He describes Duryodhana as wicked, proud and convinced of victory, backed by Bhishma, Drona and Karna and by kings who fear Krishna. He argues that Krishna's words will be wasted on such men and asks him not to walk into a hostile assembly.

scenes.B05C092S01: Vidura warns Krishna during the night that Duryodhana is wicked and overconfident and that his counsel will be ignored.

shots.B05C092S01H01: Vidura warns Krishna at night that his visit is ill-judged, since Duryodhana is wicked, overconfident and backed by the kings, and that his counsel will be ignored.

B05C093.summary: Krishna answers Vidura that he knows Duryodhana's wickedness but goes anyway, since a sincere attempt at peace earns merit even if it fails. He argues that a friend should be pulled back from ruin and that his conscience will be clear if the Kauravas refuse. He then lies down to sleep.

scenes.B05C093S01: Krishna replies that he will try for peace despite Duryodhana's wickedness, then goes to sleep.

shots.B05C093S01H01: Krishna answers Vidura that although he knows Duryodhana's wickedness, he goes to make peace, since a sincere attempt earns merit and a friend should be pulled back from ruin.
shots.B05C093S01H02: Vaisampayana says Krishna lies down on his soft bed to sleep.

B05C094.summary: At dawn Krishna performs his rites, gives gifts to Brahmanas, and rides in procession through the decorated streets to the Kuru court. The kings rise to honour him, and he greets Dhritarashtra and Bhishma, and asks that the Rishis who have come down from the sky be given seats. Once Krishna is seated, the whole assembly falls silent.

scenes.B05C094S01: Krishna rides to the Kuru court, is honoured by the assembly, and the Rishis who have come to watch are given seats.

shots.B05C094S01H01: At dawn Krishna bathes, worships the sun, gives gifts to Brahmanas, and receives Duryodhana and Sakuni, who tell him the court is waiting.
shots.B05C094S01H02: Krishna rides in a grand procession through the decorated streets to the Kuru court, where the kings rise to honour him, he greets Dhritarashtra and Bhishma, asks that the Rishis led by Narada be seated, and the assembly falls silent.

B05C095.summary: Krishna addresses Dhritarashtra before the whole assembly and urges peace to avoid the slaughter of heroes. He asks the king to restrain Duryodhana and give the Pandavas their share of the kingdom, recalling their loyal exile and the Kauravas' dice fraud. He warns of the ruin war would bring, and the assembled kings silently approve, though none dares speak against Duryodhana.

scenes.B05C095S01: Krishna urges Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons and grant the Pandavas their share, warning of ruin, and the kings silently approve.

shots.B05C095S01H01: Krishna urges Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons, warns that war means wholesale slaughter, and says the Pandavas ask only for their lawful share of the kingdom.
shots.B05C095S01H02: Vaisampayana says the kings silently applaud Krishna's words but none dares speak in front of Duryodhana.

B05C096.summary: Rama, son of Jamadagni, tells the Kuru court the parable of King Dambhodbhava, who boasted of his strength until he sought battle with the ascetics Nara and Narayana. Nara defeated him with blades of grass, and the humbled king learned restraint. Rama then reveals that Nara and Narayana are now Arjuna and Krishna, and urges Duryodhana to make peace.

scenes.B05C096S01: Rama tells Duryodhana the parable of a proud king defeated by the sage Nara, then urges peace with the Pandavas.

shots.B05C096S01H01: Rama tells the parable of King Dambhodbhava, who, proud of his power, sought battle with the ascetics Nara and Narayana and was turned away by them.
shots.B05C096S01H02: Nara defeats the king with blades of grass and teaches him humility, and Rama tells Duryodhana that Nara and Narayana are now Arjuna and Krishna, urging him to make peace.

B05C097.summary: The sage Kanwa adds his counsel to Duryodhana: only Vishnu is eternal, while all else, kings included, is perishable and reborn. He urges Duryodhana not to trust in mere strength and to make peace with Yudhishthira. He then tells the tale of Matali's search for a husband for his daughter Gunakesi, which ends with Matali entering the world of the Nagas.

scenes.B05C097S01: Kanwa urges Duryodhana to make peace, then tells the story of Matali searching for a husband for his daughter.

shots.B05C097S01H01: Vaisampayana says the sage Kanwa speaks to Duryodhana after the words of Jamadagni's son.
shots.B05C097S01H02: Kanwa says only Vishnu is eternal while all else perishes, urges Duryodhana to make peace and not trust mere strength, and begins the tale of Matali searching for a husband for his daughter Gunakesi.
shots.B05C097S01H03: Matali finds no suitable husband among gods or men, consults his wife, and sets off for the world of the Nagas.

B05C098.summary: Kanwa continues the tale of Matali's search. Narada meets Matali on the road, learns his errand, and takes him down to Varuna's realm to look for a groom. There Narada describes the marvels of the Naga world, including Varuna's son Pushkara, the weapons of defeated Daityas, and a bow that gave Arjuna's Gandiva its name.

scenes.B05C098S01: Narada and Matali travel to Varuna's realm, where Narada describes its marvels, including a bow linked to Arjuna's Gandiva.

shots.B05C098S01H01: Kanwa says Narada meets Matali on the way, learns his errand, and takes him to Varuna's realm to look for a groom.
shots.B05C098S01H02: Narada describes Varuna's realm, including his son Pushkara, the weapons of defeated Daityas, Vishnu's discus, and a bow said to be the source of Arjuna's Gandiva, and then suggests moving on.

B05C099.summary: Narada shows Matali the city of Patala and its marvels, including a fire fed by water, the moon's healing rays, Airavata's rain, and a mysterious egg that has no known origin. Matali finds no suitable groom there and asks to leave. The chapter then turns to a new section.

scenes.B05C099S01: Narada describes the wonders of Patala, and Matali rejects the region as unsuitable for a groom.

shots.B05C099S01H01: Narada shows Matali the city of Patala and its marvels, including a fire fed by water, the moon's rays, Airavata's rain and an egg of unknown origin, but Matali finds no suitable groom and asks to leave.

B05C100.summary: Narada shows Matali Hiranyapura, the Danava city built with illusions and guarded by mighty demons who could not be defeated by the gods. He describes their mansions and treasures, and asks Matali to look for a groom there. Matali refuses to seek a match among the enemies of the gods and asks to move on.

scenes.B05C100S01: Narada shows the Danavas' city of Hiranyapura, and Matali refuses to seek a groom among enemies of the gods.

shots.B05C100S01H01: Narada shows the Danavas' city of Hiranyapura, with its illusions and mighty demons, and Matali refuses to seek a groom among enemies of the gods.

B05C101.summary: Narada takes Matali to the realm of the birds, the sons of Garuda, who feed on snakes but revere Vishnu. He names their many chiefs and offers to move on to another region if none of them suits. The chapter continues the catalogue of possible grooms.

scenes.B05C101S01: Narada describes the realm of the birds, the sons of Garuda, and their chiefs, then offers to move on.

shots.B05C101S01H01: Narada presents the realm of the birds, the sons of Garuda, who feed on snakes and revere Vishnu, names their chiefs, and offers to move on if none suits.

B05C102.summary: Narada describes Rasatala, the home of Surabhi, mother of cows, whose milk formed the Milky Ocean. He explains that her offspring cows support the four quarters of the world, and that her milk becomes food suited to each kind of being. He quotes an old verse praising Rasatala above all other realms.

scenes.B05C102S01: Narada describes Rasatala, the home of Surabhi, and the origin of the Milky Ocean.

shots.B05C102S01H01: Narada describes Rasatala, the home of Surabhi, mother of cows, whose milk formed the Milky Ocean and whose offspring support the quarters, and quotes an old verse praising the place.

B05C103.summary: Narada describes Bhogavati, the Naga city ruled by Vasuki, where Shesha holds up the earth and countless Nagas dwell. Matali notices a young Naga standing by Aryaka and asks about him, saying he would make a fine husband for Gunakesi. Narada reveals the youth is Sumukha, grandson of Aryaka, whose father Chikura was killed by Garuda, and Matali is pleased to choose him.

scenes.B05C103S01: Narada describes Bhogavati and its Nagas, and Matali picks out the young Naga Sumukha as a groom for his daughter.

shots.B05C103S01H01: Narada describes Bhogavati, ruled by Vasuki, where Shesha holds up the earth and countless Nagas dwell, and names many of them, inviting Matali to look for a groom.
shots.B05C103S01H02: Matali, looking at a youth who stands beside Aryaka, asks about his parentage and says he would make the best husband for Gunakesi.
shots.B05C103S01H03: Narada tells Matali the youth is Sumukha, grandson of Aryaka, whose father Chikura was killed by Garuda, and Matali says he is pleased to offer his daughter to him.

B05C104.summary: Narada praises Matali and asks Aryaka to accept Sumukha as a groom for Gunakesi. Aryaka hesitates, because Garuda killed his son and has threatened to devour Sumukha within a month. Matali takes the matter to Indra's court, where Vishnu suggests a gift of Amrita, but Indra grants Sumukha only long life, and the marriage goes ahead.

scenes.B05C104S01: Matali's plan wins Sumukha's marriage to Gunakesi, with Indra granting him long life rather than immortality.

shots.B05C104S01H01: Narada praises Matali and asks Aryaka to give his grandson Sumukha in marriage to Gunakesi.
shots.B05C104S01H02: Aryaka is torn between joy and sorrow, fearing Garuda, who killed his son and has threatened to devour Sumukha within a month.
shots.B05C104S01H03: Matali proposes taking Sumukha to Indra's court, and the group goes to heaven, where Vishnu is also present and Narada tells the story.
shots.B05C104S01H04: Vishnu asks Indra to grant Sumukha immortality, but Indra gives him only a long life, and Sumukha marries Gunakesi and returns home, pleasing the others.

B05C105.summary: Garuda, furious that Indra has spared the Naga Sumukha and so cheated him of his food, boasts that he is as strong as the gods' king. Vishnu presses one arm on him, humbling him, and then restores Sumukha to his breast so that the two become friends. Kanwa applies the lesson to Duryodhana, warning him to avoid battle with the Pandavas and to trust in Krishna, but Duryodhana scoffs and says fate rules him.

scenes.B05C105S01: Garuda, angry at Indra, is humbled by Vishnu; Kanwa applies the lesson to Duryodhana, who scoffs at it.

shots.B05C105S01H01: Garuda, furious that Indra has spared Sumukha, complains of being disgraced and boasts that he is as strong as the king of the gods.
shots.B05C105S01H02: Vishnu presses one arm on Garuda, who collapses under the weight and begs forgiveness; Vishnu pardons him and sets Sumukha on his breast, and the two become friends.
shots.B05C105S01H03: Kanwa warns Duryodhana that he will survive only so long as he avoids battle with the Pandavas, and says Krishna is Vishnu himself, the bearer of the discus.
shots.B05C105S01H04: Duryodhana laughs, slaps his thigh, and says he is what fate made him, dismissing the sage's words.

B05C106.summary: Janamejaya asks why Duryodhana's friends and elders did not restrain him. Vaisampayana replies that Krishna, Bhishma and Narada all counselled him, and Narada tells the tale of Galava, an obstinate disciple of the sage Viswamitra. The story shows how refusing good counsel brings disgrace and trouble.

scenes.B05C106S01: Janamejaya asks why no one restrained Duryodhana, and Narada tells the tale of Galava and the sage Viswamitra.

shots.B05C106S01H01: Janamejaya asks why Duryodhana's friends and elders did not restrain him.
shots.B05C106S01H02: Vaisampayana says that Krishna, Bhishma and Narada all counselled Duryodhana, and that he will now report what they said.
shots.B05C106S01H03: Narada warns against obstinacy and tells the tale of Galava, who kept pressing his teacher Viswamitra for a fee until Viswamitra demanded eight hundred special horses.

B05C107.summary: Galava is stricken with grief and remorse at being unable to repay his teacher, and resolves to end his life. He resolves instead to seek Vishnu's protection, when his friend Garuda appears and offers to carry him across the sea to find the horses.

scenes.B05C107S01: Galava, unable to find the horses, laments and resolves to seek Vishnu, when Garuda appears and offers help.

shots.B05C107S01H01: Galava, unable to find the eight hundred horses, laments his ingratitude and resolves to seek Vishnu's protection, when his friend Garuda appears and offers to carry him across the sea to help.

B05C108.summary: Garuda offers to show Galava the world, beginning with the eastern quarter. He describes it as the gate of day and time, where the sun rises, the gods were first anointed, and the Vedas were first sung. He asks whether Galava would prefer to go there or to hear about another quarter.

scenes.B05C108S01: Garuda describes the eastern quarter as the source of the sun, the Vedas and the gods' prosperity, and offers to take Galava there.

shots.B05C108S01H01: Garuda offers to show Galava the eastern quarter, praising it as the source of the sun, the Vedas and the gods' prosperity, and asks whether another direction would suit him better.

B05C109.summary: Garuda describes the southern quarter, given as a gift by Vivaswat to his teacher and home to the ancestors and to Yama's realm. He recounts many tales of kings, sages and sinners associated with it, including the river of the dead and the city of Bhogavati. He asks whether Galava wants to go there or hear about the west.

scenes.B05C109S01: Garuda describes the southern quarter, the realm of the ancestors and of Yama, and asks which way Galava wishes to go.

shots.B05C109S01H01: Garuda describes the southern quarter, home of the ancestors and of Yama's realm, with its tales of ancient kings and sages, its river of the dead and the city of Bhogavati, and asks whether Galava wants to go there or hear of the west.

B05C110.summary: Garuda describes the western quarter, the realm of Varuna, where the sun sets and the sea is said to begin. He recounts its wonders, including the defeat of the Daityas, the Maruts' birth and the home of Vishnu and Kasyapa. He then asks Galava which way they should go.

scenes.B05C110S01: Garuda describes the western quarter, Varuna's realm, and asks Galava to choose the direction.

shots.B05C110S01H01: Garuda describes the western quarter, Varuna's realm where the sun sets and the sea begins, and where Vishnu, Kasyapa and other figures dwell, and asks which way Galava would choose.

B05C111.summary: Garuda describes the northern quarter as the most sacred direction, where Krishna and Arjuna dwell at the Vadari hermitage and Shiva rests on the Himalayas. He lists its wonders, including the Ganges falling from heaven, Kuvera's realm, the sages who guard the river's source, and Vishnu's footprint. He then offers to show Galava any quarter he likes.

scenes.B05C111S01: Garuda describes the northern quarter, its sacred sites and the sages who guard the source of the Ganges.

shots.B05C111S01H01: Garuda describes the northern quarter as the most sacred direction, where Krishna and Arjuna dwell at Vadari, Shiva rests on Himavat, and the Ganges falls from heaven, and lists many marvels there.
shots.B05C111S01H02: Garuda describes the sages who guard the Ganges' source, Vishnu's footprint, King Marutta's sacrifice and the gold mines of Himavat, then says the north is superior to every other quarter and offers to show Galava all of them.

B05C112.summary: Galava asks Garuda to carry him east, where the gods and virtue are said to dwell. The flight is so fast that Galava is terrified by the storm and the sparks, and he despairs of ever finding the steeds, saying death seems the only way out. Garuda laughs at him and proposes they rest on Mount Rishabha.

scenes.B05C112S01: Galava asks to be carried east, is terrified by the flight, and despairs; Garuda laughs and suggests a rest on Mount Rishabha.

shots.B05C112S01H01: Galava asks Garuda to carry him to the eastern quarter, where the gods and virtue are said to dwell.
shots.B05C112S01H02: Galava, riding on Garuda's back, praises his speed, describes the storm and the sea creatures, begs him to slow down, and says he has no wealth to pay his pledge and sees only death ahead.
shots.B05C112S01H03: Garuda laughs, says death is ordained by God and cannot be brought on by effort, and proposes they rest on Mount Rishabha.

B05C113.summary: On Mount Rishabha they honour the ascetic lady Sandili and eat her food, after which Garuda wakes to find his wings gone. He admits he had wished to carry her off, and she forgives him on condition he never looks down on women, then restores his wings. The steeds still cannot be found, and Viswamitra meets Galava and demands his fee.

scenes.B05C113S01: Garuda loses his wings after resting with Sandili, is forgiven and restored, and Viswamitra demands the fee again.

shots.B05C113S01H01: Garuda and Galava rest on Rishabha and eat Sandili's food, then wake to find Garuda's wings gone; after he admits he wanted to carry her off, Sandili forgives him and restores his wings, and when the steeds cannot be found, Viswamitra demands his fee again.

B05C114.summary: Garuda tells Galava that wealth must be begged from a king, and proposes King Yayati of Pratisthana, a descendant of Nahusha. When they reach the court, Yayati welcomes them, and Garuda explains how Galava has been sent by Viswamitra to fulfil his fee.

scenes.B05C114S01: Garuda explains that wealth must come from a king and proposes King Yayati, who welcomes them and hears Galava's story.

shots.B05C114S01H01: Garuda explains that wealth must be sought from a king, proposes King Yayati of Pratisthana, and when they reach his court, Yayati welcomes them and hears Galava's story of his debt to Viswamitra.

B05C115.summary: Yayati, though poorer than Garuda supposes, refuses to send Galava away empty-handed and offers his daughter Madhavi as a gift to pay the debt. Garuda departs, and Galava takes Madhavi to King Haryyaswa of Ayodhya, seeking a dower for her.

scenes.B05C115S01: Yayati, unable to meet the full need, gives his daughter Madhavi to Galava, who then goes to King Haryyaswa.

shots.B05C115S01H01: Yayati, though poorer than Garuda supposes, gives his daughter Madhavi to Galava to pay the debt; Garuda departs, and Galava takes her to King Haryyaswa of Ayodhya, asking him to accept her with a dower.

B05C117.summary: Galava takes Madhavi to Divodasa, king of Kasi, and asks him to father a son by her. Divodasa agrees to one son but says his wealth cannot cover the steeds. Narada lists many divine and royal couples, and Madhavi bears Pratardana; when Galava returns, Divodasa gives her back as agreed.

scenes.B05C117S01: Galava brings Madhavi to Divodasa, who agrees to father one son, and Narada lists celebrated couples of the gods and kings.

shots.B05C117S01H01: Galava introduces Madhavi to Divodasa, king of Kasi, and asks him to beget a child by her.
shots.B05C117S01H02: Divodasa agrees to father one son, says his wealth cannot cover the steeds, and Narada lists many divine and royal couples; Madhavi bears Pratardana, and when Galava returns, Divodasa gives her back as promised.

B05C116.summary: Haryyaswa admires Madhavi, but when Galava asks for eight hundred steeds he has only two hundred. Madhavi suggests four kings could each give steeds for one son, and Haryyaswa takes her for a single son, Vasumanas. When Galava returns for the balance, Haryyaswa cannot pay, so he gives Madhavi back, and Galava moves on to King Divodasa.

scenes.B05C116S01: Haryyaswa admires Madhavi, takes her for one son, and then returns her when Galava comes back for the rest of the dower.

shots.B05C116S01H01: Narada describes Haryyaswa's admiration of Madhavi's beauty and his question about her dower, and Galava's demand for eight hundred steeds.
shots.B05C116S01H02: Haryyaswa says he has only two hundred of the steeds; Madhavi proposes four kings give steeds for four sons, and Galava agrees to a fourth of the dower for one son, who is born as Vasumanas.
shots.B05C116S01H03: When Galava returns for the balance, Haryyaswa cannot make up the six hundred steeds, returns Madhavi, and Galava takes her on to King Divodasa.

B05C118.summary: Madhavi, again a maiden, goes with Galava to King Usinara of the Bhojas. Galava asks for four hundred steeds for two sons, and Usinara, who has only two hundred of the right kind, agrees to father one son, Sivi. Galava then takes Madhavi back and goes to see Garuda.

scenes.B05C118S01: Galava takes Madhavi to King Usinara, who fathers one son, Sivi, and Galava then returns to Garuda.

shots.B05C118S01H01: Galava takes Madhavi to King Usinara of the Bhojas, who agrees to father one son, Sivi, in return for part of the steeds, after which Galava takes her back and goes to see Garuda.

B05C119.summary: Garuda tells Galava that the missing steeds cannot be found, since the kings bought them from Brahmanas and some were lost in a river. He advises Galava to offer Madhavi to Viswamitra as the remaining price, and Viswamitra accepts her, fathers a son, Ashtaka, and receives the six hundred steeds. Galava then returns Madhavi to her father and goes into the woods.

scenes.B05C119S01: Garuda sends Galava to Viswamitra with Madhavi and the steeds, and Madhavi bears Ashtaka.

shots.B05C119S01H01: Garuda tells Galava the missing steeds cannot be found, so he should offer Madhavi to Viswamitra, who accepts her, fathers Ashtaka and takes the six hundred steeds, after which Galava returns her to her father and goes into the woods.

B05C122.summary: Yayati is recognised by the virtuous kings and rises back to heaven. Each of his four grandsons gives him the merit of his good deeds: Vasumanas his liberality, Pratardana his valour, Sivi his truthfulness, and Ashtaka his sacrifices. Yayati ascends on their gifts, and the kings declare themselves his daughter's sons.

scenes.B05C122S01: Yayati is recognised and rises to heaven as his grandsons each give him the merit of their deeds.

shots.B05C122S01H01: Yayati rises back to heaven as each of his grandsons, Vasumanas, Pratardana, Sivi and Ashtaka, gives him the merit of his good deeds, and they declare themselves his daughter's sons.

B05C123.summary: Yayati returns to heaven with honours and asks why his merit was exhausted. Brahma replies that vanity alone caused his fall, and that pride and contempt for others are the greatest sins. Narada then turns the lesson to Duryodhana, urging him to give up pride and wrath and make peace with the Pandavas.

scenes.B05C123S01: Yayati is restored to heaven, Brahma explains that his fall came from vanity, and Narada turns the lesson to Duryodhana.

shots.B05C123S01H01: Yayati returns to heaven with honours and asks why his merit was exhausted, and Brahma replies that vanity alone caused his fall and warns against pride and contempt for others.
shots.B05C123S01H02: Narada tells Duryodhana that Yayati's vanity and Galava's obstinacy both led to ruin, and urges him to abandon pride and wrath and make peace with the Pandavas.

B05C120.summary: King Yayati brings Madhavi to a swayamvara at a sacred hermitage, but she passes over all suitors and chooses the forest as her lord, living as an ascetic like a deer. Years later Yayati grows proud in heaven and disregards the gods and sages. None there recognise him, and he loses his splendour.

scenes.B05C120S01: Madhavi rejects all suitors at Yayati's swayamvara and chooses an ascetic life in the forest, and Yayati later falls from heaven through pride.

shots.B05C120S01H01: Yayati brings Madhavi to a swayamvara at a sacred hermitage, where she passes over all suitors and chooses the forest as her lord, living as an ascetic like a deer.
shots.B05C120S01H02: After many thousands of years, Yayati grows proud in heaven, disregards the gods and sages, and when questioned, none recognises him, and he loses his splendour.

B05C121.summary: Yayati, stripped of his heavenly glory, is hurled from heaven, and he asks to fall among the righteous. He lands among four kings holding a sacrifice in Naimisha, who ask who he is. Madhavi arrives and tells her father her sons will save him, and Galava offers an eighth of his austerities to help him back to heaven.

scenes.B05C121S01: Yayati, hurled from heaven, lands among four kings holding a sacrifice in Naimisha, and Madhavi arrives with her sons and Galava to help him back to heaven.

shots.B05C121S01H01: Yayati is hurled from heaven, wishes to fall among the righteous, and lands among four kings holding a sacrifice in Naimisha, who ask who he is.
shots.B05C121S01H02: Madhavi arrives, is greeted as mother by the four kings, tells Yayati her sons will save him, and Galava offers an eighth of his austerities to help him back to heaven.

B05C124.summary: Dhritarashtra tells Narada he agrees with his counsel but has no power to make Duryodhana follow it. He asks Krishna to persuade his son, and Krishna gives a long plea for peace, urging Duryodhana to obey his father, make peace with the Pandavas, and stop relying on weak allies. Krishna warns that no one can defeat Arjuna, and that the Kauravas will be destroyed if they go to war.

scenes.B05C124S01: Dhritarashtra asks Krishna to persuade Duryodhana, and Krishna gives a long plea for peace.

shots.B05C124S01H01: Dhritarashtra tells Narada he agrees with the counsel but cannot make his son follow it.
shots.B05C124S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks Krishna to persuade Duryodhana, and Krishna warns him at length to make peace with the Pandavas, obey his father, drop his reliance on weak allies, and recognise that no one can beat Arjuna.

B05C125.summary: Bhishma and Drona urge Duryodhana to heed Krishna and make peace, warning that the Pandavas cannot be beaten and that war will destroy the Bharata race. Vidura grieves for the aged Dhritarashtra and Gandhari, who would be left to wander as beggars. Dhritarashtra begs his son to accept Krishna's offer of reconciliation.

scenes.B05C125S01: Bhishma, Drona, Vidura and Dhritarashtra each plead with Duryodhana to accept Krishna's offer of peace.

shots.B05C125S01H01: Bhishma and Drona urge Duryodhana to accept Krishna's counsel and make peace, warning that Arjuna is greater than any man and that the Pandavas cannot be defeated.
shots.B05C125S01H02: Vidura grieves for the aged parents, who would be left to beg if Duryodhana persists, and Dhritarashtra begs his son to be reconciled with Yudhishthira through Krishna.

B05C126.summary: Bhishma and Drona plead once more with Duryodhana. They list the terrible scenes of war that have not yet begun, such as Krishna and Arjuna arming for battle and Bhima raising his mace, and urge him to make peace before those scenes come true. They ask him to embrace Yudhishthira and his brothers, who will embrace him in return.

scenes.B05C126S01: Bhishma and Drona list the horrors of war that have not yet begun and urge Duryodhana to make peace.

shots.B05C126S01H01: Bhishma and Drona plead again, listing the disasters of war that have not yet begun, and urge Duryodhana to make peace while there is still time, embracing the Pandavas as brothers.

B05C127.summary: Duryodhana angrily answers Krishna that he alone is blamed, that the Pandavas accepted the dice game, and that he has already returned the stolen wealth. He refuses to bow to the Pandavas, or even to Indra, and says he will not give them back even a needle's point of land while his father lives. He declares that a Kshatriya should die on the battlefield rather than yield.

scenes.B05C127S01: Duryodhana angrily refuses Krishna's terms, saying he will not yield a needle's point of land while his father lives.

shots.B05C127S01H01: Duryodhana angrily answers Krishna that the Pandavas accepted the dice game, that he will not bow to them or give back even a needle's point of land while his father lives, and that a Kshatriya should die on the battlefield rather than yield.

B05C128.summary: Krishna rebukes Duryodhana for his crimes against the Pandavas, from the dice game and the insult to Draupadi to the attempts to burn and poison them. Dussasana threatens that the Kauravas will bind Duryodhana and hand him over to the Pandavas. Duryodhana storms out, and Krishna urges the elders to bind him, citing old examples of wicked men who were restrained for the good of all.

scenes.B05C128S01: Krishna rebukes Duryodhana, Dussasana threatens to bind him, and Duryodhana storms out of the court, while Krishna urges that he be bound.

shots.B05C128S01H01: Krishna rebukes Duryodhana for the dice game, the insult to Draupadi, and the plots to burn and poison the Pandavas, and urges him to give them their share.
shots.B05C128S01H02: Dussasana tells Duryodhana that if he will not make peace, the Kauravas will bind him and hand him over to the Pandavas.
shots.B05C128S01H03: Duryodhana storms out with his brothers and counsellors, Bhishma says his enemies will rejoice, and Krishna urges the elders to bind him, citing the defeat of the Daityas and Kansa, and to make peace.

B05C129.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura to fetch Gandhari, hoping she can persuade their son. Gandhari blames her husband for indulging Duryodhana, then pleads with her son to restrain his greed and wrath, make peace with the Pandavas, and accept Krishna's counsel. Vidura brings Duryodhana back, and the chapter closes with the next section heading.

scenes.B05C129S01: Gandhari pleads with Duryodhana to restrain his greed and wrath and make peace with the Pandavas, and Duryodhana is brought back to the court.

shots.B05C129S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura to fetch Gandhari, hoping she can persuade their son to make peace.
shots.B05C129S01H02: Gandhari blames Dhritarashtra for indulging their son and asks that Duryodhana be brought before her without delay.
shots.B05C129S01H03: Vidura brings Duryodhana back into the court, angry and breathing hard, and Gandhari rebukes him for treading the wrong path.
shots.B05C129S01H04: Gandhari urges Duryodhana at length to obey his father and elders, master his lust and wrath, make peace with the Pandavas, and accept Krishna's protection.

B05C130.summary: Duryodhana, with Karna, Sakuni and Dussasana, plots to seize Krishna first. Satyaki overhears the plot and warns Krishna and the elders, and Krishna says he will not stoop to violence even if the plotters try. Dhritarashtra then orders Duryodhana back into the court, rebukes him, and Vidura recalls Krishna's feats to show that no one can seize him.

scenes.B05C130S01: Duryodhana plots to seize Krishna, Satyaki warns the court, and Dhritarashtra and Vidura rebuke the prince, recalling Krishna's feats.

shots.B05C130S01H01: Duryodhana and his allies plot to seize Krishna, Satyaki learns of it and warns Krishna and the elders, and Krishna says he will not stoop to violence even if they try.
shots.B05C130S01H02: Dhritarashtra orders Vidura to bring Duryodhana back into the court to make one more attempt at persuading him.
shots.B05C130S01H03: Dhritarashtra rebukes Duryodhana, calling his plan an infamous folly that no one, not even the gods, could carry out against Krishna.
shots.B05C130S01H04: Vidura recalls Krishna's past feats, from the attack at Saubha to the defeat of Naraka and Kansa, to show that no one can seize him by force.

B05C131.summary: Krishna mocks Duryodhana's plan to seize him and reveals a dazzling universal form, from which gods, heroes and his own allies appear. Most of the kings are terrified, though Drona, Bhishma and Vidura hold firm. Dhritarashtra then protests his good faith, and Krishna takes leave of the elders and rides to Kunti's house in full view of the Kurus.

scenes.B05C131S01: Krishna answers Duryodhana's plot with a display of his universal form, then takes leave of the elders and rides to Kunti.

shots.B05C131S01H01: Krishna mocks Duryodhana, reveals a dazzling universal form filled with gods and heroes that terrifies the kings, and then Dhritarashtra protests his good faith.
shots.B05C131S01H02: Krishna takes leave of Dhritarashtra and the elders, mounts his chariot, and drives to the house of his aunt Kunti in view of the Kurus.

B05C132.summary: Krishna reports the failure of his mission to Kunti and asks what message she wants him to take to the Pandavas. Kunti urges Yudhishthira to act as a Kshatriya and fight rather than live on alms. She cites the example of Muchukunda and the power of kings to bring about a good or bad age, and warns that shirking battle brings shame.

scenes.B05C132S01: Krishna reports to Kunti, who sends Yudhishthira a message urging him to fight as a Kshatriya.

shots.B05C132S01H01: Krishna reports to Kunti that the court has refused peace and asks what message she would like him to take to the Pandavas.
shots.B05C132S01H02: Kunti tells Krishna to urge Yudhishthira to fight as a Kshatriya, citing Muchukunda and the king's power over the age, and warns him against living on alms.

B05C133.summary: Kunti tells an old tale of the warrior mother Vidula, who scolds her defeated son for lying down in despair. Vidula calls him a coward and urges him to rise and fight, saying that a man who avoids battle is no true man. The son replies that he has no use for the earth without his mother's favour, and she answers that a brave man should support others by his own strength.

scenes.B05C133S01: Kunti tells the tale of Vidula, who scolds her defeated son and urges him to fight bravely.

shots.B05C133S01H01: Kunti introduces an old tale of Vidula and her son and says Yudhishthira should learn from it.
shots.B05C133S01H02: Vidula, a proud and learned woman, scolds her son for lying defeated after losing to the king of the Sindhus, calls him a coward, and urges him to rise and fight.
shots.B05C133S01H03: The son says the earth and life mean nothing to him without his mother's favour, and Vidula replies that a true man supports his friends by his own prowess and lives by his own strength.

B05C134.summary: Vidula continues her rebuke, telling her son that a Kshatriya who avoids battle is like a thief and that his fame depends on fighting. She recalls a Brahmana's prophecy that the son would one day regain greatness, and urges him to win back the kingdom. She argues that sovereignty is the door to heaven, and says a Kshatriya must bow only to Brahmanas.

scenes.B05C134S01: Vidula continues to scold her son, telling him a Kshatriya who avoids battle is a thief, and urging him to fight for his kingdom.

shots.B05C134S01H01: Vidula continues to scold her son, telling him that a Kshatriya who avoids battle is like a thief, recalling a Brahmana's prophecy of his future greatness, and urging him to fight bravely, since sovereignty is the door to heaven.

B05C135.summary: In Kunti's tale, Vidula scolds her son for his despair and tells him a Kshatriya is made for battle, and that shirking action brings shame. The son replies that he lacks wealth and allies and asks what he can do. Vidula urges him to act with energy, win over the wronged and the angry, and treat his followers generously.

scenes.B05C135S01: Vidula scolds her son for his despair, and he asks what he can do with no wealth or allies.
scenes.B05C135S02: Vidula urges her son to act, gain allies and treat his followers well.

shots.B05C135S01H01: The son replies to his mother, calling her harsh and asking what use the earth and his life would be to her without him.
shots.B05C135S01H02: The mother replies that the wise act for virtue and profit, that a Kshatriya is made for battle, and that a son who shirks action brings shame.
shots.B05C135S01H03: The son asks his mother to show him kindness and to stop speaking so harshly.
shots.B05C135S01H04: The mother says she is pleased to hear it and will keep urging him until he wins.
shots.B05C135S01H05: The son says he has no wealth or allies and asks his mother to tell him the means of success.
shots.B05C135S02H01: The mother urges him that failure is no reason to despair, that he must rally the angry, weakened and humbled to his side with gifts and kind words, since a king who joins his foe can never regain his kingdom.

B05C136.summary: Vidula tells her son that a king in distress must not betray his cause, since his friends and loyal followers will stand by him. She offers him hidden treasure and faithful allies. The son's despair lifts, and he vows to win back his kingdom or perish in the attempt. Kunti then says this tale of Jaya should be read to any king who is down.

scenes.B05C136S01: Vidula tells her son that friends and hidden treasure remain to him, and his despair lifts; Kunti recommends the tale to others.

shots.B05C136S01H01: Vidula tells her son that a king in distress must not give up, that his friends remain loyal, and that she will give him hidden treasure and faithful allies.
shots.B05C136S01H02: Kunti says her son's despair lifts, and he vows to rescue his kingdom or die in the attempt, while keeping his mother's words in mind.
shots.B05C136S01H03: Kunti says a minister should read this tale of Jaya to any king in distress, as it breeds courage and a brave son for any mother who listens.

B05C137.summary: Kunti gives Krishna a message for each of her sons. She recalls a celestial voice that foretold Arjuna's victory and the recovery of the kingdom, urges Bhima and the twins to act as warriors, and reminds all of Draupadi's insult. She asks Krishna to protect her sons. Krishna takes leave of Kunti, speaks with Karna, and drives swiftly back to Upaplavya, while the Kurus lament Duryodhana's folly.

scenes.B05C137S01: Kunti gives Krishna messages for her sons and Draupadi, and Krishna departs for Upaplavya after speaking with Karna.

shots.B05C137S01H01: Kunti asks Krishna to deliver her message: a celestial voice foretold Arjuna's victory, Bhima and the Pandavas should act as warriors, Draupadi's insult must be remembered, and Krishna should protect her sons.
shots.B05C137S01H02: Krishna takes leave of Kunti, dismisses the Kuru chiefs, takes Karna on his chariot, and the Kurus marvel at what they have seen and blame Duryodhana's folly.
shots.B05C137S01H03: Krishna talks with Karna on the road, sends him back, and his fast steeds carry him to Upaplavya.

B05C138.summary: Bhishma and Drona warn Duryodhana that Kunti's words will be heeded, since the Pandavas now have Arjuna, Bhima, Gandiva and Krishna on their side. They recall Arjuna's past feats at Virata and in the cattle raid, and list the evil omens of coming slaughter. They beg Duryodhana to make peace and embrace Yudhishthira and his brothers.

scenes.B05C138S01: Bhishma and Drona warn Duryodhana of the Pandavas' strength and the omens of ruin, and beg him to make peace.

shots.B05C138S01H01: Bhishma and Drona warn Duryodhana that the Pandavas will not give up without their share, list Arjuna's past feats and the omens of ruin, and beg him to make peace and embrace Yudhishthira and his brothers.

B05C139.summary: Duryodhana says nothing, cheerless and with his face cast down. Bhishma laments that he must fight Yudhishthira, a man devoted to his elders and free of envy. Drona confesses his deep love for Arjuna but says his duty as a warrior forces him to fight him, and he urges Duryodhana to make peace.

scenes.B05C139S01: Duryodhana stays silent, and Bhishma and Drona each lament that they must fight the Pandavas, urging peace.

shots.B05C139S01H01: Duryodhana says nothing and looks cheerless, and Bhishma and Drona exchange glances before speaking again.
shots.B05C139S01H02: Bhishma says it grieves him to fight Yudhishthira, who serves his elders, is free of envy, and speaks the truth.
shots.B05C139S01H03: Drona says he loves Arjuna more than his own son, laments that his duty forces him to fight him, and urges Duryodhana to make peace with the Pandavas, whose allies are formidable.

B05C140.summary: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what Krishna said to Karna during their ride out of the city. Sanjaya reports that Krishna revealed Karna to be Kunti's firstborn son, and so the eldest of the Pandavas by birth. Krishna urges Karna to join his brothers and be crowned king, with Yudhishthira serving as his heir.

scenes.B05C140S01: Dhritarashtra asks what Krishna told Karna, and Sanjaya reports Krishna's offer to make Karna king among the Pandavas.

shots.B05C140S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what Krishna said to Karna as he took him out of the city.
shots.B05C140S01H02: Sanjaya agrees to repeat Krishna's words exactly, both the stern and the gentle parts.
shots.B05C140S01H03: Krishna tells Karna he is by birth the son of Kunti and Pandu's eldest, so he should join the Pandavas and be crowned king, with Yudhishthira as his heir, and the Pandavas and Vrishnis serving him.

B05C141.summary: Karna declines Krishna's offer. He says he was raised by the charioteer Adhiratha and cannot abandon Duryodhana, who made him king, and he asks Krishna to keep their talk secret. He then describes the coming war as a great sacrifice, with Arjuna as the Hotri, Gandiva as the ladle and the dead as the offerings. He prays that the Kshatriyas die at Kurukshetra and asks Krishna to bring Arjuna before him in single combat.

scenes.B05C141S01: Karna declines Krishna's offer, describes the war as a sacrifice, and asks Krishna to bring Arjuna to him in single combat.

shots.B05C141S01H01: Karna thanks Krishna, explains that he was raised by Adhiratha and is tied to Duryodhana, and asks Krishna to keep their talk secret, since Yudhishthira would refuse a kingdom if he knew. He then describes the coming battle as a great sacrifice, with Arjuna, Bhima, Yudhishthira, the twins and others as its priests, and the slaughter and final bath as its rites.
shots.B05C141S01H02: Karna prays that the Kshatriyas perish at Kurukshetra and asks Krishna to bring Arjuna before him for battle, keeping their discussion a secret.

B05C142.summary: Krishna answers Karna with a smile, telling him that the Pandavas' victory is already certain. He points to Arjuna's banner and the signs that the Krita, Treta and Dwapara ages will vanish in battle. He sends word to Drona, Bhishma and Kripa that the season is good and the battle should begin on the new moon, a day ruled by Indra.

scenes.B05C142S01: Krishna tells Karna that victory will be the Pandavas', citing omens, and sets the battle for the new moon.

shots.B05C142S01H01: Krishna answers Karna that victory is certain for the Pandavas, describes Arjuna's banner and the signs of their triumph, and sends word to Drona, Bhishma and Kripa that the battle should begin on the new moon.

B05C143.summary: Karna answers Krishna that the destruction of the earth is at hand, and lists omens of defeat for the Kauravas, drawn from planets, animals, birds and the state of the camp. He then describes a vision in which the Pandavas triumph and the Kauravas go to Yama. Krishna replies that when a man cannot accept good counsel, his doom is near. Karna embraces Krishna, saying they will meet again in battle or in heaven, and Sanjaya reports that Karna went back in gloom.

scenes.B05C143S01: Karna lists omens of the Kauravas' defeat and a vision of Pandava triumph, then embraces Krishna and returns in gloom.

shots.B05C143S01H01: Karna tells Krishna that a great slaughter is coming, and lists omens of defeat for the Kauravas, from the planets and the animals to the birds, drums and the sky.
shots.B05C143S01H02: Karna describes a vision in which the Pandavas rule the earth and Bhima devours it with his mace, Arjuna sits on a white elephant, and the Kurus are consumed in the fire of Gandiva.
shots.B05C143S01H03: Krishna replies that when a man's heart cannot accept right counsel, the destruction of all creatures is near.
shots.B05C143S01H04: Karna answers that they will meet again if they survive the battle, or else in heaven.
shots.B05C143S01H05: Sanjaya reports that Karna embraced Krishna, descended from his car when dismissed, and rode back in deep dejection.

B05C144.summary: After Krishna leaves, Vidura tells Kunti that Duryodhana will not hear reason and that war is near. Kunti laments the coming slaughter of kin, and recalls the mantra Durvasa gave her in girlhood, which she used to summon the sun god Surya and conceive Karna. She goes to the Ganga, where Karna is at prayer, and resolves to reveal the truth to him.

scenes.B05C144S01: Vidura tells Kunti that war is near, and Kunti goes to the Ganga to find Karna.

shots.B05C144S01H01: Vidura tells Kunti that Duryodhana refuses peace, that the Pandavas are waiting at Upaplavya, and that war now looms over the Kurus.
shots.B05C144S01H02: Kunti laments the coming war, recalls the mantra Durvasa gave her and how she summoned Surya in girlhood, then goes to the Ganga and stands in the shade of Karna's garment while he finishes his prayers to the sun.

B05C145.summary: Karna meets Kunti at the Ganga and asks what she wants of him. Kunti reveals that he is her firstborn son by Surya, not Radha's or Adhiratha's, and urges him to join the Pandavas and take his place among them.

scenes.B05C145S01: Karna asks Kunti's purpose, and Kunti reveals he is her son by Surya and urges him to join his brothers.

shots.B05C145S01H01: Karna introduces himself as the son of Radha and Adhiratha and asks what Kunti wants him to do.
shots.B05C145S01H02: Kunti tells Karna he is her son by Surya, not Radha's, born with his natural armour in her father's palace, and urges him to join the Pandavas as a true Partha and take his place among his brothers.

B05C146.summary: Kunti makes a final plea for Karna to join the Pandavas, and a voice from the sun god Surya backs her. Karna refuses, citing his loyalty to Duryodhana, his honor, and the wrong Kunti did him by abandoning him at birth. He promises that Kunti will keep five sons either way, since he will spare the other Pandavas and fight only Arjuna, and then mother and son part.

scenes.B05C146S01: Surya's voice supports Kunti, but Karna refuses to desert Duryodhana and promises to spare four of Kunti's sons.

shots.B05C146S01H01: A voice from the sun, which the text says is Surya's, tells Karna to follow his mother's words.
shots.B05C146S01H02: Karna refuses, listing his grievances against Kunti and his duty to the Kauravas, and promises to fight Arjuna while sparing the other Pandavas for now.
shots.B05C146S01H03: Kunti embraces him, says the Kauravas will fall by fate anyway, and asks him to keep his pledge in mind in battle; they part with blessings.

B05C147.summary: Krishna returns from Hastinapura and reports to the Pandavas, who ask him to repeat exactly what was said in the Kuru assembly. He repeats Bhishma's speech, in which Bhishma explains how the throne passed through Santanu's line and how his own vow shaped that line. Bhishma concludes that Pandu's sons are the rightful heirs and that Duryodhana should give them half the kingdom.

scenes.B05C147S01: Krishna reports his failed mission to the Pandavas, and Yudhishthira asks him to recall the full speeches of the Kuru assembly, starting with Bhishma's.

shots.B05C147S01H01: Krishna returns to Upaplavya and reports to the Pandavas, who meet after sunset and ask him to repeat what he said to Duryodhana.
shots.B05C147S01H02: Yudhishthira asks Krishna to recall exactly what Bhishma, Drona, Dhritarashtra, Vidura, and the other kings said in the assembly.
shots.B05C147S01H03: Krishna repeats Bhishma's speech, which tells how Duryodhana laughed at his words, recounts the royal family's history, and urges Duryodhana to give half the kingdom to the Pandavas.

B05C148.summary: Drona backs Bhishma and tells Duryodhana to give the Pandavas half the kingdom, since righteousness brings victory.
